A cold front moved through on July 29th 2023 kicking waves up to around 3 feet during the afternoon. Winds relaxed to around 1 foot at the time of the incident, but lingering currents were still present. Witnesses stated the father and son were struggling to fight the currents, which were likely a combination of rip and longshore currents as winds were northeast during the event. The son was rescued by a nearby jet skier, but the father was unable to hold on and later drowned.

This tornado started in Adams county and moved southeastward into Marquette county at the intersection of 1st Ave. and Glen Ave., and dissipated just north of STH 23, mid-way between 3rd Ave. and Neenah Creek.  It resulted in minor damage to 4 residential homes, minor damage to 2 agricultural buildings, major damage to 2 agricultural buildings, and destroyed 1 agrcultural building.  Total residential damage was about $100K and total agricultural damage was about $200K.  Some corn crop was also damaged.  The lat/long starting location in Marquette County was  43.68597/-89.59951, and the ending location was 43.66950/-89.56055.  DI#1 (SBO), DOD6.  Winds estimated at 100 mph. This tornado was extremely wide since the thunderstorm cloud base was very low and the meso-cyclone that is usually aloft was well-formed all the way to the ground.  Within a broad 1 to 2 mile wide area of EF0 to EF1 damage, there were several small swaths of EF2 damage due to multiple votices.  The accompanying graphic shows this effect.  With respect to residential homes this tornado resulted in very minor damage to 150, minor damage to 30, major damage to 10, and 2 were destroyed (total residential damage of $2 million).  With respect to agricultural buildings ($500K in total damage), this tornado resulted in minor damage to 20, and major damage to 2 buildings (inlcuding silos).  Tens of thousands of trees were uprooted or chewed-up, and many power-lines and power-poles were either toppled or damaged.  About 4000 to 6000 trees on a tree farm were destroyed at a location about 3 miles east-southeast of Pardeeville.  This tree-farm loss was treated as a crop loss.  Additionally, some corn and soybean crops were damaged.  This tornado started just southeast of the intersection of CTH P and Pardeeville Road, and moved southeastward for about 4 miles and then traveled east-southeast to end just northeast of the western intersection of STH 146 and CTH A.  The specific starting point and ending point lat/long numbers were 43.53333/-89.26306 and 43.49556/-89.09878, respectively.  Additional mid-point pairs of number include: 43.51603/-8922394, 43.50728/-89.20151, and 43.50208/-89.17679. DI#24 (ELT), DOD4.  The wind speeds were estimated at about 120 mph.  Average path length was about 1760 yards (1 mile).

Sauk County experienced 4 flash flood events over a 3-day period.  Two of the events started on June 7th, one on June 8th, and the last one on June 9th.  In each case, flash flooding caused home and business damage as well as crop losses.  Roads were blocked or washed out (STH 154 and CTH C), and bridges were damaged.  Many vehicles stalled.  Locations in the Baraboo River Valley sustained considerable damage as the river crested at all-time levels.  Collectively, each of these 4 flash floods resulted in home and business damage along with some crop losses.  It was nearly impossible to break down the damages by flash flood event.  Therefore, the collective breakdown is provided in the June 9th StormData entry for Sauk County.

Beginning section of the second tornado to ever occur in February in Wisconsin.  Storm chaser/spotter/public videos show the tornado beginning around 5:39pm south of Evansville.  The tornado intensified as it tracked to the east of Evansville where it impacted 30 primary residences (2 destroyed, 10 major impacts, 13 minor impacts, 5 affected).  Numerous barns and outbuildings were destroyed along the path as it tracked to the northwest of Edgerton.  The main EF-2 damage was confined to a stretch from east of Evansville to just southwest of the Yahara River.  There was one person in a car that was hit by the tornado that had injuries serious enough to warrant transportation to the hospital, but they were deemed minor and released.  Almost every person that was impacted by the tornado that the damage surveyors talked to said that they received the warning via Wireless Emergency Alert on their cell phone and then went to their shelter to gather more information via TV, radio, social media.  County wide estimates of damage was at about $2.5 million.

For the Dane County portion of this tornado, it was mainly at EF-1 intensity and entered the county just to the northwest of Edgerton and exited on the northwest side of Lake Koshkonong.  It went through the far south side of Albion and appeared to cross Interstate 39 just north of the Highway 73 exit.

This portion of the tornado was also mainly EF-0 or EF-1 type damage as it tracked along the north side of Lake Koshkonong through Busseyville.  A few barns and outbuildings made of sheet metal had damage to them along with one residence.

This weak tornado spun up in the rural area roughly mid-way between New Glarus and Postville, just northeast of Zentner Road about 0.8 miles north-northwest of the intersection of CTH H and Zentner Road. It moved northeast, clipping the northwest part of the city of New Glarus, and exited Green County going through the western edge of the city of Belleville.  Luckily only uprooted trees or snapped-off tree damage was noted.  This tornado finally dissipated about 2 miles south-southeast of the village of Paoli in south-central Dane County near CTH A.  The path length was about 7.84 miles in Green County and 4.41 miles in Dane County, for a total path length of about 12.25 miles.  The starting and ending locations in Green County, with respect to lat/long pairs of numbers, were 42.80215/-89.69455 and 42.85690/-89.55898. DI#27 (TH), DOD3.  Wind speeds estimated at 83-87 knots (95-100 mph).  Average path width in Green County was about 75 yards.

It entered Dane County on the west side of the city of Belleville and then moved northeast through the Lake Belle View area and drossed STH 69 about 1 mile north of the county line, and ultimately dissipated southeast of Basco, near CTH A.  Luckily only tree damage occurred - of the uprooted tree or broken tree branch variety. The tornado began just west of Murray Rd, north of Bass Creek where portions of several trees were snapped. The tornado quickly grew, moved to the east-northeast and produced damage rated EF-1 neighborhoods near Loch Lomond park. EF-2 damage was noted at a residence on the east side of county highway D where well over one hundred trees were snapped or uprooted. The tornado continued to the northeast, crossing the Rock River, Highway 11 and Highway 51 producing damage rated EF-1. The second area of EF-2 damage was noted a neighborhood just northwest of Burbank Park, where a house lost its roof and a portion of its second story. The roof was found to the north-northwest over a block away. The tornado continued northeast crossing Beloit Ave. and ending in the fields to the west of South Read Rd. Damage along the majority of the path was rated EF-1. Tree damage was substantial with well over 1000 trees that were snapped, uprooted or had large sections damaged. Roof damage on several structures included shingle loss, occasional loss of roof decking material, peeled or dislodged siding and other facia and soffit peeling and removal. A few structure sustained damage to walls when their garage doors were breached. Numerous power poles were leaning, with several snapped.

Scattered tree limbs down, some large, along highway 14 from just east of Mazomanie to just west of Middleton after a series of lines and clusters of thunderstorms.

Floodwaters affect homes and boat docks in the Blackhawk Island area of Lake Koshkonong on the north side of the lake. Floodwaters spread over low spots on Blackhawk Island Road in the area where the Rock River enters the lake.

Water surrounds seasonal homes along Old River Rd. in the Blackhawk Park area including water at the base of Caledonia/Lewiston Levee on Old River Rd. Old River Rd., W Lake Rd., Sec K Rd., and Blackhawk Rd. are all covered with water. West Lane Rd. in the Long Lake area has 4 feet of water over it in places. Farther south in the Town of Dekorra, about 12 homes are flooded on Hwy V. Water also over River Oaks Rd. and Oak Knoll Rd. near Hwy V.
There is widespread flooding of agricultural land and lowland. There is widespread flooding in Riverbend Campground, about 5 miles upstream of Milford.

The city of Waupun sewer plant was flooded with many reports of sewage backups in basements. The city issued a disaster declaration for the flooding. Floodwaters reached the support beams underneath the Fond du Lac St. bridge and it was closed. Gateway Dr. just east of Fond du Lac St. is closed. Upstream, water starts to over top the dam at Shaler Park. Yet farther upstream, County Park Rd. at the bridge is closed. Otherwise, floodwaters affect a park and many other roadways adjacent to the river.
Floodwaters are over Tritz Rd. near Hwy 33 and I-90, as well as impacting parking lots to businesses in the same area. There is widespread flooding of agricultural land.

Following the flash flooding earlier in the evening, the flooding of Spring Creek in Lodi affected Goeres Park, including the pool and baseball diamond. A little farther downstream, floodwaters affected Habermann Park, and farther downstream yet the water approaches the Public Works garage. There was standing water in many low lying areas and streets in Lodi, but also throughout southwest and west central Columbia County. This included sections of Poynette and Arlington as well as portions of highway Q and CS.

Floodwaters affect a road in Riverside Park on the north side of Janesville and South River Road on the south side of Janesville. Floodwaters affect a home on South Christian Road on the east side of the river in the Afton area. There is extensive lowland and agricultural land flooding in the Afton and Janesville areas.
In the Avon Bottoms area, there is flooding in Sugar River Park, and Beloit Newark Rd. and S. Hopkins Rd.

Damage reports from two local storm chasers showed a tornadic path southwest of Evansville.  Video from a resident on the SW side of Evansville showed the tornado moving through mainly farmland, which was confirmed via satellite and ground surveys.  Main damage was to a wheat field and a tree line.

Moderate street flooding in portions of Janesville including the intersection of Bond Place and Waveland Road. Farther west, street flooding and sandbagging operations on highway B northwest of Footville, but the water drained fairly quickly.

Flowing water over small portions of rural roads due to flooding of farm fields or ditches. This included high water over a portion of highway A between Footville and Janesville, and several inches of water on Townline Road near Avon. A roof collapsed in Edgerton due to the accumulation and weight of rain water. Urban street flooding also prevalent.
Flowing water from open fields and residential yards across portions of Lake Drive and into Lake Koshkonong. Flooding basements reported.

Flooding of several basements and yards on the west side of Iron Ridge when a culvert became plugged. The electricity was shut off until the water receded. The flooding of a creek eroded the shoulder of County Highway AY near Madison Road, just east of Iron Ridge. A business dock was flooded in Horicon.
A culvert partially undermined by floodwaters on County Highway DG northeast of Fall River. A washed out shoulder northbound on Highway 146 south of Cambria.

A swath of straight-line wind damage from the Oconomowoc area to 4 miles north of Merton. The Oconomowoc Lake Police Department reported widespread tree damage across the village. Over 100 trees were snapped or uprooted with every road in the village either completely or partially blocked. Farther to the northeast, numerous trees were downed on the west side of Pine Lake with scattered tree and powerline damage elsewhere across the path of high winds. A measured wind gust of 63 mph was taken at the intersection of highway 67 and I-94 at 10:09 PM CST, but maximum winds around 70 mph were estimated in the village of Oconomowoc Lake.
Numerous reports of street flooding in the Madison area. A couple of streets closed due to high water with estimated depths of 8-10 inches.

Random pockets of tree damage blown down in a divergent pattern on the west side of Lake Mary and Elizabeth Lake . Powerlines down as well.
A couple public reports of street flooding and standing water in New Glarus.

Several roads flooded throughout the county, especially in the Baraboo and North Freedom areas and in low lying areas. Portions of some roads and culverts partially washed out. A railroad bridge was damaged in Devils Lake State Park. Lake Delton and Prairie Du Sac also reported street and yard flooding. Some of the roads in low lying areas remained flooded well into the next day.

Street and road flooding in northern Dane County including some road damage. Some homes affected by flooding in Windsor, Medina, and Sun Prairie. A culvert failed in Windsor. Lowland flooding throughout the area.
Street and road flooding in portions of the county including in Pardeeville, Lodi, and water flowing over County Highway P near Cambria. Lowland flooding throughout the area.

The flooding of the Crawfish River resulted in portions of River Rd. and Campbell St. flooding near the highway 16/60 bridge. The high river stage was impacting the bottom portion of the bridge. Neighborhood yards flooded in the vicinity of the river.

Flooded creek flowing over County Highway K between Country Club Rd. and Wardsville Rd. A flooded Pecatonica River flowing across Ferndale Rd. between County Highway C and King Rd. Lowland flooding throughout the area.
Street flooding on several streets in Waupun and Beaver Dam, including backyard and basement flooding.

Street and road flooding in southern and eastern Fond du Lac County with some road closures needed. This included the communities of Eden, Byron, Oakfield, and Alto. Some road washouts have occurred. Basement flooding as well. Flooding at a campground in the Kettle Moraine. Lowland flooding throughout the area.
Significant street flooding in Orfordville at highway 11 and 213, and just north of Footville, and in the city of Janesville. Other street flooding reported in and near Beloit   and Clinton.
Fast moving water over County Highway P between Pompey Rd. and Anderson Rd. from a flooding creek.

A brief, weak tornado spun up in a rural area southeast of Manchester, and uprooted or damage trees, pulled a roof off a pole shed, damaged the overhang and roofing of a residential home's garage, and damaged a part a small part of another home's roof.  This tornado spun up just southeast of Lake Maria, and moved east-northeast across CTH O about 1/2 mile north of the county line, and then dissipated in open fields.  Some corn crop was also damaged.  The starting and ending lat/long pairs of numbers were:  43.63654/-88.98887 and 43.64454/-88.96897.  DI#2 (FR12), DOD4.  Winds were estimated at 97 mph, and the average path width was about 40 yards.

It took the roof off of a lumberyard pole shed, took part of a roof off an office building, uprooted trees, and brought down some power-lines.   The starting and ending lat/long pairs of numbers are 43.65243/-89.21794 and 43.65347/-89.19503.  DI#1 (SBO), DOD 5.  The winds were estimated at 93 mph.  The average path width was about 50 yards.

Water flowing over a portion of highway 126 near Belmont. Portions of roads flooded in or near Benton, Shullsburg, Darlington, South Wayne and Gratiot. A culvert washed out near Benton.

Heavy rains of 2 to 3 inches within 1 to 1.5 hours resulted in flash flooding in and around Benton as water depths reached 3 feet on some roads.  Some gravel shoulder washouts were noted.

A series of thunderstorms dumped 2 to 4 inches of rain in Sauk County that resulted in flash flooding.  Several county roads were closed due to fast-flowing water depths of 1 to 2 feet.  Basement flooding was noted, and there was some shoulder gravel washouts.  A semi-tractor trailer stalled in deep water on a road near Loganville after the current pushed the truck off the road, and the driver had to be rescued.

A series of thunderstorms dumped heavy rains that resulted in fast-flowing water depths of 1 to 3 feet on urban strees. One person in Madison had to be rescued when their car stalled in 3 feet of water. Several roads were closed due to high water levels. Basement flooding was noted with damage to contents.

Many roads closed due to high water on the east side of the county with some shoulder washouts. More specifically, there was scouring of pavement and shoulder material on County Road E just south of the Norwegian Creek bridge.
Water had flowed over portions of highway 59 and highway 104 in far western Rock County. Water also had flowed over the intersection of County Road A and Old 92.
Street flooding in Kenosha and Pleasant Prairie with water up to the bottom of vehicles.

Numerous funnel clouds were reported across central Rock County. The locations were from just east of Brodhead to near Orfordville, Footville, Janesville, and just south of Milton. No tornadoes occurred.

Many tree limbs snapped off a large tree and landed on a home. A combination of fallen tree limbs and straight line winds tore at least a 100 square foot section of siding from the home. Other damage to siding, fascia, gutters, and a broken window.
Scattered trees down in Whitewater, Richmond, and the Sugar Creek area.
A barn destroyed and trees down.

A series of thunderstorms dumped 1 to 3 inches of rain across the city of Janesville.  Several roads become flooded with fast-flowing water to the depth of 1 to 3 feet.  Several cars stalled in the deep water and drivers had to be rescued.  Some basement flooding was noted with damage to contents.

A line of severe storms moved west to east across Sheboygan County and generated widespread powerful winds that gusted to an estimated 61 to 70 knots (70 to 80 mph).  In addition, a tornado spun up north of Sheboygan Falls at 1437 CST - see the tornado event write-up for deatils.  The ASOS unit at the Sheboygan County Airport measured a gust of 53 knots (61 mph).  Thousands of trees were snapped or toppled, and many power-lines were brought down by tree debris, mostly across the northern part of the county.  An 81-year-old women in Plymouth was injured when the winds pushed a door of a store into her.  She broke her arm and was hospitalized.  Elsewhere in Plymouth, 2 vehicles were damaged by tree debris.  North of Plymouth, 2 cabins at a camp ground were destroyed by toppled trees, and 3 other camp buldings were damaged.  In Sheboygan Falls, at least 12 homes were damaged.  In Kohler, a vehicle was crushed by a toppled tree.  City and county 911 Communications Centers received thousands of calls within a 5 hour period. At least 14,000 homes in Sheboygan County lost electrical power.
Powerful thunderstorm winds toppled many large trees in a wide path of about 10 miles, and broken tree branches brought down some power-lines.  One vehicle in Beaver Dam was damaged by tree debris.

This tornado spun up on the front side of a line of thunderstorms in association with a strong microburst that rotated around on itself.  It damaged an airport hangar door, destroyed 3 barns, damaged 2 other barns, lightly damaged 3 homes, took the top 1/3 of a silo down, damaged 2 other silos, and uprooted or snapped many trees.  Only some minor corn crop damage was noted.  It was observed by several people.  This tornado started on the east side of the Sheboygan County Airport, and moved east-southeast and eventually crossed STH 32 about midway between STH 23 and CTH O.  Once it crossed STH 32 it curved sharply to a south-southeast bearing and dissipated northeast of the intersection of STH 23 and STH 32.  It's starting and ending pairs of lat/long numbers were: 43.76517/-87.84273 and 43.75375/-87.81711.  DI#1 (SBO), DOD6.  The winds were estimated at about 95 mph.  The average path width was about 30 yards.
Street flooding on the south side of Sheboygan, including removed manhole covers from flooding sewers. Pictures of streets and yards flooded on the south side.

Heavy rains of 1 to 2 inches in an hour resulted in flash flooding at generated fast-flowing water depths of 1 to 2 feet on several roads.  Additonal sandbagging was noted in Reedsburg.  Water was reported in some basements leading to damage of contents.  Some roads were closed.

Powerful downburst straight-line winds toppled many large trees.  Tree debris knocked down some power-lines.

An isolated severe storm moved south-southeast through the Princeton area and generated wind gusts that uprooted some trees and knocked many tree branches.  Hail up to 1/2 inch in diameter was also reported.

Powerful thunderstorms winds knocked down a few large trees, andn blew down some tents at the annual Strawberry Festival.  Two people at the festival were injured by broken tree branches and received medical treatment for minor injuries.

This weak tornado started in Columbia County, northeast of the village of Fall River near the county line, just northwest of the intersection of Raven Road and Hemling Road.  It moved southeastward and crossed into Dodge County where a creek crosses the county line just southeast of Paul Road.  Minor tree damage was noted in Columbia County.  The starting and ending locations for the Columbia County segment, with respect to lat/long pairs of numbers, were 43.41413/-89.01782 and 43.41086/-89.00504.  DI#27 (TH), DOD2.  Wind speeds estimated at 65 mph.  Average path width was about 15 yards.

This weak Dodge County tornado started in Columbia County, northeast of Fall River near the county line.  It moved southeast and entered Dodge County where a creek crosses the county line about 1/2 mile north-northwest of the intersection of STH 73 and CTH D.  This tornado resulted in only minor tree damage in Dodge County.  The starting and ending locations for the Dodge County segment, with respect to lat/long pairs of numbers, were 43.41086/-89.00504 and 43.40230/-88.97749.  DI#27 (TH), DOD2.  Wind speeds estimated at 65 mph.  Average path width was about 15 yards.

This tornado started in Columbia County about 6 miles southeast of Cambria, or about 3 miles south of Randolph, or about 1/3 mile west of the intersection of CTH CD and Court Road.  This tornado crossed into Dodge County where Beaver Creek crosses the county line Only minor tree damage was noted in Columbia County.  The starting and ending locations for the Columbia County segment, with respect to lat/long pairs of numbers, were 43.49298/-89.01509 and 43.49473/-89.00625.  DI#28 (TS), DOD2.  Wind speeds estimated at 75 mph.  Average path width was about 15 yards.

This Dodge County tornado started in Columbia County, about 6 miles southeast of Cambria, and crossed into Dodge County where Beaver Creek crosses the county line.  It moved east-northeast to point where CTH FW makes its closest approach to Rakes Bay. It then dissipated over the middle of Rakes Bay.  In Dodge County, a home was damaged, a barn was severely damaged, and the top part of a silo was knocked off.  Many large trees were uprooted and branched broken off.  Also, some corn and soybean fields were damaged.  The starting and ending locations for the Dodge County segment, with respect to lat/long pairs of numbers, were 43.49473/-89.00625 and 43.50617/-88.96057.  DI#1 (SBO), DOD5.  Wind speeds estimated at 95 mph.  Average path width of the Dodge County segment was about 50 yards.

Heavy rains resulted in flash flooding from the Endeavor area to the Montello area.  Water depths on road surfaces reached 3 feet or more and there were gravel washouts.  One hundred homes were affected with at least some flooding. Two hundred homes had minor damage.  Eighty-five homes had major damage, and one home was destroyed (total of 6 million for all home property losses).  Fifty businesses had minor damage, 10 had major damage, and 1 was destroyed (total of 750 thousand for all business property losses).  Crops losses were estimated at 2 million.  Public sector damage was about $2 million.  There were several roads and bridges that sustained damage.

Heavy rains resulted in flash flooding from the Cobb to Arena area.    Water depths on road surfaces reached 3 feet or more and there were gravel washouts.  At least one hundred homes were affected with at least some flooding.  Ninty-five homes had minor damage, and 5 homes were destroyed (total of $1.5 million for all home property losses).  No business losses were reported.  Crops losses were estimated at $500 thousand.  Public sector damage was about $1.325 million.  There were several roads and bridges that sustained damage.

Heavy rains resulted in flash flooding from the Darlington area to Yellowstone Lake State Park.  Water depths on road surfaces reached 3 feet or more and there were gravel washouts.  Home damage totaled about $200 thousand.  Business damage totaled about $100 thousand.  Crop losses totaled about $300 thousand.  Public sector damage totaled about $162,160.  There were several roads and bridges that sustained damage.

Heavy rains resulted in flash flooding from the Mequon area northeast to the Belgium to Port Washington area.  Water depths on road surfaces reached 3 feet or more and there were gravel washouts.  One hundred twenty-seven homes had minor damage, and 191 homes had major damage (total of $3.765 million for all home property losses).  Business losses were about $810 thousand.  Crops losses were estimated at $500 thousand.  Public sector damage was about $1.1 million.  There were several roads and bridges that sustained damage.

Heavy rains resulted in flash flooding across much of the northwest half of the county.  Water depths on road surfaces reached 3 feet or more and there were gravel washouts.  Two hundred thirty-nine homes had minor damage, 9 homes had major damage, and 26 were destroyed (total of $7.46 million for all home property losses).  Fifty-four businesses had minor damage, and 24 had major damage (total business losses were about $810 thousand.  Crops losses were estimated at $15 million).  Public sector damage was about $10.3 million.  There were several roads and bridges that sustained damage.

Heavy rains led to widespread flash flooding around the city of Fond du Lac.  The river flowing through downtown rose out of its banks up to the bridges and most roads were under 2 to 4 feet of water.  Several vehciles stalled in the deep water and sustained water damage.

Heavy rains led to flash flooding that generated water levels of 2 to 4 feet deep on many low-lying roads, especially near existing lakes.  Several vehicles stalled in the deep water and were damaged.  A 68-year-old man left a tavern around 2245 CST and drove into a flooded area.  He attempted to walk/swim away from his vehicle and drowned.

Track started southwest of Lowell and ended south of Juneau.  Damage was mainly to about 30 trees, but there was barn damage along Fairwood Rd near the onset of the tornado and some roofing panels lofted from the Animix facility south of Juneau near the end of the tornado path.

Extensive damage path from this tornado which started southwest of Juneau, went through the north side of downtown Juneau, to the south of Horicon, hitting the Horicon Hills Golf Club, before ending east of Horicon along Highway 33.  The most intense damage was in the city of Juneau where about 10 structures hit EF-2 levels of damage.  The one minor injury from this tornado occurred in downtown Juneau where a man was sleeping in his bedroom when the roof blew off and a tree fell into the house.  The Clearview facility had windows blown out and one housing building lost it's roof.  Another residential building, which looked like a motel, lost a long section of its roof, but was poorly attached to the frame of the building. An empty silo was buckled on the east end of Home Rd with one cow having a two by four impaled into its back.  At the Horicon Hill Golf Club, 165 trees were either uprooted or damaged extensively.  Numerous golf carts were tipped or displaced and the main club house sustained extensive roof damage.

Tornado began on the north end of the Dodge County Airport, damaging 5 airport hangars and one airplane. The tornado continued east and went through the far south side of Horicon near River Bend Park, causing mainly tree damage along the rest of its path along with some minor barn and housing damage.

Tornado began southwest of Mayville just west of Highway 28 which was also captured on video as a potential multi-vortex tornado.  Some of the more intense damage occurred shortly after the tornado developed and crossed County Rd TW on into southwest Mayville in an industrial area.  A farmhouse on Cty RW lost a portion of its roof and some farm sheds. The tornado then moved through the industrial area in southwest Mayville.  The Mayville Engineering Company was hit on its northwest corner.  The winds from the tornado breached a large garage door on the west side which then pushed the large north end wall down.  The tornado then went through the Gleason Reel Corporation and destroyed the southern portion of the building.  It then went through a neighborhood near the St. John/Graceland cemetary before crossing Main St/Rock River.  The tornado then went through the east side of Mayville near the Mayville Golf Course.  It then continued to the northeast through mainly rural areas before ending NW of Theresa.
Damage began northeast of the roundabout for Highway 28 and 175 which is separate from the Mayville tornado.  Damage was mainly to trees along this path that crossed Interstate 41.
Tornado started southwest of Lomira and north of County Rd AH.  While briefly on the ground, it destroyed a barn west of Highway 67.

events.event_narrative: An EF-1 rated tornado developed near the Farm and Fleet in Dodgeville, first moving northeast through a corn field.  The tornado then continued to the northeast, impacting numerous trees and one outbuilding.  The strongest damage occurred off of County Road ZZ, where numerous large, healthy hardwood trees were uprooted.  The tornado ended near Knobs Road, just west of County Road H.

The main area of damage was to the Birchwood Drive neighborhood where about 20 to 40 trees were uprooted or had multiple limbs broken off.  Multiple storm chaser videos show the main tornado tracking just along and to the west of this neighborhood. The only structural damage noted that wasn't from falling trees was to one house on Birchwood Drive that had a few shingles pulled up.

Brief tornado that occurred in a corn field north of Beaver Dam west of Buckhorn Road.  Reports from emergency management and storm chasers in the area was that the tornado lasted about 20 seconds.  Satellite imagery confirmed the tornado path cutting across two corn fields while hitting one tree.

Tornado developed south of Hustisford near the intersection of Hillcrest Road and County Road E where a corn field had a convergent path going north-northeast through mainly farmland.  The tornado hit some trees south of Highway 60 and east of County Road E before tracking north and going through the intersection of Juneau Street and Oakwood Boulevard.  The tornado appears to have ended over Sinissippi Lake.

Widespread flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods and homes occurred especially in New Berlin, Brookfield, Butler, Menomonee Falls, Elm Grove, and Muskego. Some of the more notable creeks or rivers that flooded were the Fox and Menomonee Rivers and their tributaries. The Butler Ditch, Jewel Creek, Root River, and other unnamed creeks also flash flooded. For all of Waukesha County, 3 homes were classified as destroyed, 310 homes and businesses sustained major damage, 221 with minor damage and 119 with affected damage. These damages were from a variety of 1st floor flooding, basement flooding, and foundation collapse. Residential sewage backups, and raw sewage released into rivers by many municipalities were common.  A small number of complete road washouts and swift water rescues occurred, in addition to dozens of people stranded in their vehicles in deep, still water in low lying areas. More specifically, a partial road washout occurred on Lily Road in Menomonee Falls due to the flash flooding of a tributary of the Menomonee River. The large collapse of a Y-shaped intersection at Campbell Dr. and Campbell Ct. in Menomonee Falls also occurred due to the flash flooding of Butler Ditch. A car was swept away at this intersection but the occupant escaped with minor injuries. 130 St. in New Berlin was partially washed out from the flash flooding of a tributary of the Root River. A swift water rescue occurred on Beres Rd. in New Berlin when a car was swept off the road by floodwaters. Dozens of people were evacuated or relocated from their flooded homes and neighborhoods. Very brief rise into moderate flood stage along the Menomonee River at Menomonee Falls between 1-1:15 AM local time August 10.

Widespread flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods and homes occurred especially in New Berlin, Brookfield, Menomonee Falls, Waukesha, Pewaukee, Merton, and Muskego. Some of the more notable creeks or rivers that flooded were the Fox River, Jewel Creek, and their tributaries, as well as some lake flooding.  Some flood damage occurred to homes especially near Linnie Lac Lake toward Little Muskego Lake. These damages were from a variety of 1st floor flooding, basement flooding, and foundation collapse. Residential sewage backups, and raw sewage released into rivers by many municipalities were common.  A small number of complete road washouts and swift water rescues occurred, in addition to dozens of people stranded in their vehicles in deep, still water in low lying areas. More specifically, one lane of Gold Dr. washed out due to the flash flooding of Jewel Creek in Muskego. Large sections of Barker Road in Brookfield and other nearby roads were closed due to the flash flooding of the Fox River, including the Fox River overtopping the Barker Rd. bridge. Dozens of people were evacuated or relocated from their flooded homes and neighborhoods, which included the Deer Path Subdivision near Minooka Park. A sidewall of the Merton Millpond Dam was damaged but quickly repaired. Many other dams in eastern Waukesha County were at or exceeding their maximum flow capacity, but no dam failures occurred.
Some flash flooding of streets, creeks, and low lying neighborhoods in Merton, Hartland, Delafield, Oconomowoc and surrounding areas.

Flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in Germantown and surrounding areas. More specifically, the flash flooding of the Menomonee River and its tributaries flooded and closed portions of many roads. This included portions of County Line Road, a lane of I-41, Freistadt Road, Lilac Lane, Maple Road, Rockfield Road, and Wausaukee Road. There was a small number of stranded vehicles in relatively deep, still water, as well as some basement flooding in Germantown.

Flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in West Bend and other communities over northern Washington County. Some vehicles were stranded in relatively deep, still water. The neighborhoods near the Silverbrook Creek Parkway experienced the worst of the flash flooding in West Bend, as several homes suffered foundation damage, while most had basement flooding. Some sewer backups occurred in West Bend. Approximately 316 properties reported flood damage.

A continuation of flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, low lying neighborhoods, and basements in West Bend and other communities over northern Washington County. Additional showers and storms aggravated the flooding. The neighborhoods near the Silverbrook Creek Parkway in West Bend experienced severe basement flooding, but also several instances of partial foundation collapse. Approximately 316 properties reported flood damage in West Bend.

A continuation of flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, low lying neighborhoods, and basements in Germantown and surrounding communities. Additional showers and storms aggravated the flooding. Some vehicles stranded in relatively deep, still water. More specifically, the flooding of the Menomonee River and its tributaries flooded and closed portions of many roads. This included portions of County Line Road, the northbound lane of I-41, Freistadt Road, Lilac Lane, Maple Road, Rockfield Road, and Wausaukee Road. The Riversbend Circle neighborhood in southwest Germantown experienced widespread flooding with 2 to 3 feet of water on the streets, especially on Riverbend Circle W. Many homes reported basement flooding and electrical power was lost in the neighborhood. A voluntary evacuation of 48 citizens was conducted by the local government.  Overall there were about a 170 reports of flooding in Germantown. An elderly man died and his wife was hospitalized from probable carbon monoxide poisoning from a generator being run in a garage.

Widespread flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods and homes continued over the eastern half of the county and was aggravated by additional showers and storms.  The greatest concentration of flooding was in New Berlin, Brookfield, Butler, Menomonee Falls, Waukesha, Pewaukee, Merton, and Muskego. Some of the more notable creeks or rivers that flooded were the Fox River, Menomonee River, Jewel Creek, Butler Ditch, Root River, and their tributaries, as well as some lake flooding. Some flood damage occurred to homes especially near Linnie Lac toward Little Muskego Lake. These damages were from a variety of 1st floor flooding, basement flooding, and foundation collapse. Residential sewage backups, and raw sewage released into rivers by many municipalities were common. A small number of complete road washouts and swift water rescues occurred, in addition to dozens of people stranded in their vehicles in deep, still water in low lying areas. More specifically, one lane of Gold Dr. washed out due to the flash flooding of Jewel Creek in Muskego. Large sections of Barker Road in Brookfield and other nearby roads were closed due to the flash flooding of the Fox River, including the Fox River overtopping the Barker Rd. bridge. A partial road washout occurred on Lily Road in Menomonee Falls due to the flash flooding of a tributary of the Menomonee River. The large collapse of a Y-shaped intersection at Campbell Dr. and Campbell Ct. in Menomonee Falls also occurred due to the flash flooding of Butler Ditch. 130 St. in New Berlin was partially washed out from the flash flooding of a tributary of the Root River. Dozens of people were evacuated or relocated from their flooded homes and neighborhoods, which included the Deer Path Subdivision near Minooka Park and homes near Linnie Lac. A sidewall of the Merton Millpond Dam was damaged but quickly repaired. Many other dams in eastern Waukesha County were at or exceeding their maximum flow capacity, but no dam failures occurred. River flooding along the Lower Fox River in Waukesha peaks during the evening of August 11, with a 8.62 foot crest in moderate flood stage occurring at 5:15 PM local time. Moderate river flooding continues along Lower Fox River in Waukesha through the morning hours of August 13. In moderate flood stage, water from the Lower Fox River approaches the base of the Bastow St and Bank St Bridges in downtown Waukesha, in addition to some homes in the Bethesda Court area about one half mile south of downtown Waukesha. Water also inundates the Frame Park area, with waters at least 3 feet deep on land near the shoreline of the Lower Fox River. Water approaches Corrina Blvd and Union St to the south of downtown Waukesha.

The flash flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in Mequon, Thiensville, Cedarburg and southern Grafton. More specifically, the flash flooding of Pigeon Creek washed out a portion of Highland Rd. The flash flooding of Olau Creek flooded Pioneer Rd. just west of Port Washington Rd., and also flooded Port Washington Rd. just north of Pioneer Rd. The same creek flooded a portion of Bonniwell Rd. The flash flooding of the Little Menomonee River flooded a portion of County Line Rd. between Tamerland Dr. and Granville Rd. The Mequon Nature Preserve experienced flooding including its Education Center.  Other roads were closed near the flooded Milwaukee River.  At least 400 basements experienced flooding due to excessive runoff or sewer backups. Several vehicles stranded in floodwaters with some floating in relatively deep water.

The continued areal flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in Mequon, Thiensville, Cedarburg and southern Grafton. More specifically, the flooding of Pigeon Creek washed out a portion of Highland Rd. The flooding of Olau Creek flooded Pioneer Rd. just west of Port Washington Rd., and also flooded Port Washington Rd. just north of Pioneer Rd. The same creek flooded a portion of Bonniwell Rd. The flooding of the Little Menomonee River flooded a portion of County Line Rd. between Tamerlane Dr. and Granville Rd. The Mequon Nature Preserve experienced flooding including its Education Center. Other roads were closed near the flooded Milwaukee River, which included many roads in a neighborhood near the River Forest Nature Preserve. Other roads flooded and closed due to the flooding of the Milwaukee River were a portion of Green Bay Rd. in Thiensville, River Rd. from Donges Bay Rd. to County Line Rd., and Island Dr. from East Shoreland Dr. to Circle Dr. Sections of I-43 were closed due to flooding. This included I-43 northbound from Pioneer Rd. to Hwy 60. Only one lane of I-43 southbound was open. The I-43 southbound exit ramps to Grafton and Mequon Rd. were closed. Moderate flooding of the Cedar Creek at Cedarburg occurs during the morning and afternoon hours of August 12, with a crest of 11.03 feet occurring at 10:15 AM local time August 12. Moderate river flooding of the Cedar Creek at Cedarburg leads to the closure of Cedar Creek Park in downtown Cedarburg, in addition to the inundation of backyards of some homes and businesses along Sheboygan Rd in the community of Cedarburg. Moderate river flooding continues until 3 PM local time August 12.

The flash flooding of some streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in northern Cedarburg, Grafton, Saukville and Port Washington. Some basement flooding due to excessive runoff or sewer backups.

The continued areal flooding of streets, creeks, rivers, and low lying neighborhoods in northern Cedarburg, Grafton, Port Washington and other areas of central and northern Ozaukee County. Sections of I-43 were closed due to flooding. This included I-43 northbound from Pioneer Rd. to Hwy 60. Only one lane of I-43 southbound was open. The I-43 southbound exit ramp to Grafton was closed. The Milwaukee River flooded and closed Riverside Dr. north of highway 33 in Saukville as well as other roads near the river. Some basement flooding continued during this time.

The Milwaukee River and Cedar Creek continued to flood from the heavy rainfall of prior days in Ozaukee County. For the flooded Milwaukee River, floodwaters affected Island Dr. and Shoreland Parkway in the Mequon area. Water is over Elm St, Green Bay Rd., and North Cedarburg Rd. in Thiensville. The following roads and intersections are flooded and closed due to the flooding of the Milwaukee River: Portions of Blueberry Rd. and Hawthorne Dr. in the Town of Saukville, Highway W between Highway 33 and Highway 57 in the Village of Saukville. Some parks and park roads are flooded and closed in the county due to the flooded Milwaukee River and Cedar Creek.

Widespread and numerous reports of flash flooding in streets, in addition to rivers, creeks, and streams across the southern two thirds of Milwaukee County. 1800 homes were classified as major damage or destroyed due to flash flooding of the Lincoln and Honey Creeks. Many instances of flooded basements across the impacted area. Six foundations collapsed into basements of homes in the 60th street neighborhood near Lincoln Creek, with two homes being condemned. Additional basement collapse reported in West Allis near Honey Creek. Many vehicles stranded in flood waters, with multiple water rescues conducted by the Milwaukee Fire Department. Water reached the bottom of car doors at Wisconsin State Fair Park. Reports of water inside vehicles along Delaware Avenue in Bay View. Multiple runway and taxiway closures reported at Mitchell International Airport and Timmerman Field from flooding. Impacts contribute to an estimated $65,813,855 in public and individual infrastructure damages countywide.  Brief (30-45 minute total duration) rises into moderate flood stage along the Kinnickinnic River at Milwaukee and Oak Creek in South Milwaukee between 12:30 & 2:30 AM local time on August 10. At 10 feet, water impacts the yards of homes along Oak Creek in South Milwaukee. At 16 feet, flood water is approximately 1 foot over the top of the concrete-lined channel of the Kinnickinnic River at Milwaukee, affecting homes in the residential neighborhood next to the river. Homeless camp swept away as a result of rapid rises along the Kinnickinnic River, leaving some dead and missing.

Continuation of widespread flash flooding impacts occurring countywide. Delayed flash flooding onset across far northern portions of Milwaukee County, where heavy rain arrived later in the overnight hours of August 9-10, 2025. Additional numerous reports of flash flooding near rivers, creeks, and streams. Numerous reports of water in basements across the impacted area. Portion of 47th street between Churchill Ln & Willow Rd completely washed away from flooding of an unnamed creek in Brown Deer. Flooding impacts contribute to an estimated $65,813,855 in public and individual infrastructure damage across Milwaukee County.

Lingering areal flooding impacts following the conclusion of flash flooding impacts. Lingering road closures from standing water and rivers/creeks that remain out of their banks. Lingering reports of water in basements, in addition to inundation of properties from standing water. Record crest of 11.25 feet (major flood stage) occurs along the Milwaukee River at Estabrook Park at 4:15 AM local time August 10, with the river remaining in major flood stage until 9 AM local time August 10 and moderate flood stage until 11:15 AM local time August 10. In moderate flood stage, waters from the Milwaukee River at Estabrook Park lead to widespread flooding in the Glendale area, with floodwaters inundating much of Lincoln and Kletsch Parks. Numerous Glendale streets are affected by floodwaters, including but not limited to Bender Rd, West Riverview Dr, North Forest Dr, and North Sunny Point Rd. Moderate river flooding occurs at the Root River in Franklin, with a record crest of 11.71 feet occurring at 3:30 PM local time August 10, and the river remaining in moderate flood stage until 7:15 AM local time August 11. In moderate flood stage, floodwaters from the Root River at Franklin inundate the Root River Pkwy, 8 Mile Rd, 27th St, in addition to yards along the river. Floodwaters from the Root River lead to widespread flooding of agricultural land and lowlands.

Batten Airport in Racine recorded a wind gust of 67 mph. Outdoor equipment and trailers were moved across a parking lot of a large retailer, including substantial damage to its sheds. Some snapped and uprooted trees also occurred in the Racine area.

Brief tornado started south of Beaver Dam and went through a garage near Shaw Hill Rd, west of the Shaw Marsh Wildlife Area.  Other wind damage was noted on the southern side of the tornado path, attributed to downburst winds.

Tornado appears to have started west of I-39 along Church Rd where it tracked to the north side before hitting a farmstead along Highway 73.  Two metal barn structures were completely destroyed with sheet metal from these buildings found in the trees in the far farm hill to the east.  A cement silo was also lifted up and had 3 large chunks of the cap broken off of it.  The tornado appears to have gone southeast toward County Road A before ending near Woodside School Rd.  Extensive straight line/rear flank downdraft wind damage occurred about a mile or two to the south of the tornado with one farm shed destroyed along Highway 73 south of Thornson Rd.  Sheet metal from this building appeared to be tumbled into the nearby field to the east.
Continuation of the Dane County/Rockdale tornado.  Only briefly went into Jefferson county with a field tree line hit.

Tornado appeared to develop in the Lisbon Oaks subdivision, causing mainly tree damage before intensifying closer to Highway 164.  The tornado was at it's most intense near Indian Grass Lane where it caused damage to multiple businesses.  The strongest damage was to an insurance car shop port that had a well anchored roof that was completely blown off and found approximated 3 to 4 blocks to the east near Highway 164.  Damage then occurred to a church near Wildwood Way and multiple homes along Conservancy Court.  Tornado appeared to end near Waukesha Ave along Linda Dr.

The tornado started near Grouse Rd east of Briggsville and then tracked to the northeast.  The worst damage was to an onion farm south of County Road O.  The tornado crossed Interstate 39 and dissipated near County Road CX.  Storm chaser videos and photos along with security camera footage from the onion farm confirm the tornado.

The tornado started northwest of County Road ES, west of Interstate 43, south of East Troy where it heavily damaged two barns.  Corn stubble was noted to be deposited from the corn field to the west all along a path through a cemetery up to Interstate 43.  Some tree damage was noted along Alpine Valley Golf Course.  The tornado then moved along County Road D and caused additional damage to some barns and outbuildings along with numerous trees.  The tornado ended somewhere south of County Road D and northwest of Valley View Road.

The tornado developed northwest of Honey Creek Road and then hit a barn along the road, shifting it off of its foundation.  The tornado then continued southeast toward Waterford, removing sheet metal from a shed along Buena Park Rd. The tornado then continued through the north side and downtown Waterford where most of the damage was to trees and houses from the trees falling on them.  A few trees were noted to have been lofted and dropped into the Fox River.  The tornado then continued through the east side of Waterford before ending near Highway 36.
Sporadic damage path along Plank Road with mainly tree damage.  Some barn/outbuildings had damage to their roofs with sheet metal panels missing/lofted in 2 locations.

The tornado began northwest of Somers, east of Interstate 94.  It went through the north and east side of the city, through the fire department and near Somers Elementary School.  Numerous trees were uprooted along the path, some falling into houses.
The tornado began west of Quinney Road and tracked to the southeast, hitting 4 barns as it tracked across farmland west of Elkhorn.
A light glaze due to freezing rain and intermittent sleet north of Sun Prairie.
A light glaze due to freezing rain and intermittent sleet in northern portions of the county. There was a total of 0.2 inch of sleet in Oconomowoc.
A light glaze due to light freezing rain and intermittent sleet.

Snowfall totals of 10 to 11 inches and winds of 35 to 40 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. Many rural roads were impassable until the afternoon due to blowing and drifting snow. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 7 to 13 inches and winds of 40 to 50 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. There were several reports of disabled vehicle and slide-off calls reported through the county dispatch center. All schools were closed. There were 335 customers without power for a few hours in Cross Plains.

Snowfall totals of 7 to 13 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. Many rural roads were impassable until the afternoon due to blowing and drifting snow. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 8 to 16 inches and winds of 45 to 60 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. Many rural roads were impassable until the late afternoon due to blowing and drifting snow. All schools were closed. The Fond du Lac Airport ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 60 mph toward the end of the storm.

Snowfall totals of 6 to 9 inches and winds of 35 to 50 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed. The highway department for the Town of Cadiz reported that the slush followed by blowing and drifting snow made it difficult to keep the hilly North/South roads open. There were around six trees down in southwest Green County due to the winds.
Snowfall totals of 14 to 20 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed. The Government Center closed, which was a rare occasion.
Snowfall totals of 7 to 10 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 7 to 10 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. Two-foot drifts quickly developed after plowing the streets. All schools were closed. There was minor tree damage in southern portions of the county.
Snowfall totals of 3 to 6 inches and winds of 40 to 50 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.
Snowfall totals of 6 to 10 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.
Snowfall totals of 12 to 15 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 4 to 10 inches and winds of 45 to 60 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. Highest snowfall totals were in the northwest portion of the county.  The General Mitchell International Airport ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 60 mph toward the end of the storm. All schools were closed. The Interstates had difficult travel conditions and bus delays which caused the Public Libraries to be under-staffed.

Snowfall totals of 7 to 9 inches and winds of 40 to 50 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county, especially on north-south roads and open areas. Highest snowfall totals were in the northwest half of the county. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 3 to 7 inches and winds of 40 to 60 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. Highest snowfall totals were in the northwest portions of the county. The Racine Airport ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 63 mph toward the beginning of the storm. All schools were closed.
Snowfall totals of 6 to 10 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused heavy drifting and frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.
Snowfall totals of 8 to 11 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county, especially in open areas. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 7 to 12 inches and winds of 45 to 60 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. The Sheboygan Airport ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 59 mph toward the end of the storm. All schools were closed.
Snowfall totals of 6 to 8 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.
Snowfall totals of 7 to 9 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. All schools were closed.

Snowfall totals of 6 to 9 inches and winds of 35 to 45 mph caused frequent white-out conditions across the county. The Waukesha County Communications Center reported a total of 81 vehicles in the ditch or disabled or in an accident. All schools were closed.

Lightning struck a home, causing a small fire in an upstairs bedroom.
Lightning struck a garage on Cherry Lane, causing a small fire in an upstairs bedroom.  The contents was a total loss.
Lightning struck the roof of a home on Lakecrest Court.  The fire resulted in major damage and the house not inhabitable.

A swath of straight-line wind damage was observed. Dozens of trees were uprooted and widespread large limb damage occurred. A partial loss of roof shingles and fascia on several homes, and a partial loss of siding on some homes. A few small sheds were destroyed and several power lines were downed. 2200 We Energies customers were without power. The greatest concentration of damage was near the intersection of 45th Street and 38th Avenue.
Several trees and powerlines down near Whitewater.
Several trees down in the Sugar Creek Township.
An outbuilding destroyed and multiple trees down.
A portion of the Fire Department's roof torn off in North Freedom. A few mobile homes with roof damage. Several trees uprooted and many tree limbs and powerlines down. Some trees down on homes.
One silo destroyed and another heavily damaged on a farmstead. A tensile structure damaged and many trees or limbs down.
Trees down in Baraboo including on at least one home.

Numerous trees and powerlines down on the north side of Prairie Du Sac including uprooted trees. Some trees down on homes, garages and apartment buildings causing structural damage. Sheet metal removed from a portion of a roof of an industrial building.
Trees and powerlines down including some trees down on homes.
Trees down down along Delany St. and Dodgeville St. in Highland. A fallen tree causing substantial damage to the roof of a home.
Several trees down throughout the county.

Two large trees blown down and a pine tree snapped at 80 feet high in a neighborhood.  Additional trees and tree limbs down in the neighborhood and across Columbus. One tree felled on a home causing roof damage.
Dozens of trees snapped, uprooted, or downed in Lodi. Powerlines down as well. A small portion of a roof collapsed at a nursing home.
Multiple barns with roof damage, and scattered trees and powerlines down throughout the county.
Numerous trees snapped, uprooted, or downed on the north side of Cross Plains. Powerlines also down. Trees down on vehicles and homes.
Many trees uprooted and snapped in DeForest. Power poles and powerlines down. A tree down on a house. Roof damage and siding damage to some homes from the strong winds.
Snapped pine tree falling onto a home.
Numerous trees snapped about 10 to 15 feet above the ground. A felled tree onto a fiber glass roof shed, causing damage.
Multiple trees down with some down on homes and vehicles.

Around one half of the roof removed from a large church. Some roof material collapsed into the church. Across the street, a pine tree was uprooted. Another pine tree snapped halfway up and landed on a machine shed.
Some sheet metal roofing and siding torn off a barn.
Portions of a roof and beams lifted off a home.

A 1500 pound cattle gate blown over a concrete barrier at the Alliant Energy Center. A dumpster was flipped and moved a short distance. A large tensile structure was destroyed 4-5 trees blown down and 5 golf carts windshields were shattered. An AC unit was blown off the roof of a nearby hotel. Some minor roof damage to a nearby credit union.
Many trees uprooted and snapped with some falling on homes and garages. One garage was demolished.

Brief tornado that caused damage near Maple Lane southeast of Janesville.  Storm chaser video confirmed a brief tornado in this area.  More widespread damage occurred west and east of this track due to downburst winds.

Brief tornado went through Emerald Grove, destroying a barn and causing damage to an antique store.  Significant tree damage along the path as well with debris lofted well to the ENE from the structures.
Multivortex tornado documented southwest of Richmond.  Multiple sheds with sheet metal damage along County Highway M before entering Walworth County.
Multivortex tornado documented southwest of Richmond.  Multiple sheds with sheet metal damage along County Highway M before entering Walworth County.

The tornado appeared to start north of School Section Rd and west of Old 89 Rd with mainly tree damage going to the east-northeast.  The tornado then tracked along State Road 11 going east toward Delavan.  About 4 farmsteads had damage to them, including one empty silo that was blown down from about halfway up.  The tornado then continued east-southeast along Hwy 11 and ended near Redwood Ct on the west side of Delavan where it caused some tree damage.

Tornado appeared to begin along Turtle Creek west of Klug Rd and south of County Road M.  The tornado destroyed an open facing barn shed along Klug Rd.  It then tracked to the northeast and caused damage to 3 barns, a garage and a house along County Road P.  It then continued to the northeast and crossed Dam Rd before ending near Turtle Creek again.

The tornado began along Spring Prairie Rd and moved to the southeast.  The tornado had an intermittent path with a few trees uprooted, some shingles peeled from the south side of a roof, another roof peeled back on the southeast corner, and siding damage to a garage. The track continued to the southeast with several limbs snapped from the tops of trees, ending near Old County Highway DD north of Highway 11.

Tornado started in a mainly open field to the west of Highway 83.  A few branches were downed.  Along the intermittent path, multiple trees were downed in different directions.  A port-a-potty was displaced and pushed over.  The tornado continued to the northeast into an inaccessible field.

The tornado began over a farm field where a few small limbs were downed.  The tornado continued to the northeast, snapping a few trees and downing several large limbs. Further to the northeast, the view was not accessible with the tornado ending southwest of Big Muskego Lake, south of the Big Muskego Lake Wildlife area.

Tornado started near Raynor Ave and tracked to the northeast while crossing 5 Mile and 6 Mile Rd before ending near 7 Mile Rd. Most damage was minor but some sheet metal was lofted from a barn.  Tornado tracked just to the east of the Milwaukee Airport Terminal Doppler Radar.
Tornado started near 6 Mile Rd west of Raynor Ave and tracked to the northeast, ending in southern Milwaukee county.  Possible that this tornado merged with the other one directly to the south.

events.event_narrative: The Rock River at Afton rose to Moderate flood stage. Floodwaters affected Riverside Park and several blocks of Joseph and Charles Streets on the north side of Janesville and South River Road on the south side of Janesville. Traxler Park off of Memorial Drive in Janesville was flooded, including a boat ramp, and the bleachers were surrounded by water. Floodwaters surrounded a home on South Christian Rd on the east side of the river and another across the river and along W Bass Creek Rd in the Afton area. Numerous secondary roads in the Afton area were closed to traffic, and a portion of the railroad tracks near W Tripp Rd flooded. There was extensive lowland and agricultural land flooding in the Afton and Janesville areas.

The Rock River at Newville rose to Moderate flood stage. Flood waters surrounded some homes near East Mallwood Drive and were into yards and roads across eastern Newville. Floodwaters affected a riverside restaurant and its parking lot on the south side of the river.

The Rock River at Lake Koshkonong rose to Moderate flood stage. There was widespread flooding of roads and docks in the Town of Koshkonong and Town of Sumner including Vets Lane, Blackhawk Island Road and Oxbow Bend Road. There was knee-deep water over Blackhawk Island Road. Lamp Road on the west side of the river also became flooded. Lake Koshkonong merged with Mud Lake to the east of Lake Koshkonong.

The Rock River at Fort Atkinson rose to Moderate flood stage. Floodwaters partially covered low spots on Highway 106 near Rock River Park. A riverside walkway near South Water Street in downtown Fort Atkinson was closed. A few homes and businesses were surrounded by water at the end of Vets lane near the intersection of Highway 106 and Blackhawk Island Road about 1 mile southwest of Fort Atkinson. Flooded roads included Sinissippi Drive, Vets Ln, Fox Hill Rd, Bark River Road from Kutz Road to Rock River Road, Rock River Rd from Milwaukee Ave E to Hwy 106, and Ralph Rd. North Shore Road about 1 mile southwest of Fort Atkinson was closed. The river walkway in Fort Atkinson, Mechanic St boat launch, parking lot of Purdy St, yards along E Milwaukee Ave, yards on northern end of Rock River Rd, yards on Rodgers St flooded. Water backed up the Bark River into Nature Park and the parking lot. Floodwaters covered fields on the east side of Fort Atkinson.

The Fox River in Waukesha rose to a Moderate flood stage. Water touched the base of Barstow St bridge and Bank St bridge. Corrina Blvd, Buckley St, W Main St, Riverwalk Dr, and parts of Dunbar Ave flooded. Grede Park, Glacial Drumlin Trail, Fox Riverwalk, and Frame Park flooded. Floodwaters affected yards of homes near Bethesda Park.

The Fox River near New Munster in northern Kenosha County rose to Major flood stage.  Highway 50 was closed at the Fox River crossing near Hwy W. There was water on Hwy W north and south of Hwy 50. Widespread flooding occurred in the Town of Wheatland, Silver Lake and Village of Salem Lakes. Flooded roads included S 6th St, Oak St, 318th Ave, 317th Ave, 71st St, south end of 312th and 313th St, and 314th Ave. Floodwaters were into the lower levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland, Silver Lake and Village of Salem Lakes  areas along N Riverside Drive, Shorewood Drive, 101st Street and Shorewood Terrace.

The Wisconsin River at Portage rose to Major flood stage. Indian trail in Lake Delton area was flooded. Other roads that were flooded included River Oaks Road in the Town of Dekorra, River Shores Road in the Town of Lewiston, Levee Road, Cty V, Cty J, Wood Street, Summit St, Carroll, Conant St, Cty JV, and Thunderbird Road in the Portage area. Water up to Hwy 51 bridge over Duck Creek. Water approached cabins near river along Levee Rd, River Shores Rd, River Mills Rd. Sunset Point-Conant St were under water. Floodwaters affected homes in the Blackhawk Park area.

Home struck by lightning and followed by a fire. The Fort Atkinson Fire Department reported it took 45 minutes to get the fire under control. No injuries, but structural and smoke and water damage displaced the 4 residents from the home.

A swath of scattered tree, power line, and structural damage across northern Jefferson County. This included many uprooted and snapped trees, power lines down, and fallen trees on vehicles especially in Waterloo and Watertown. Eight power poles were snapped on East Clarkson Rd. in Waterloo.  A farm on highway B east of Johnson Creek suffered severe silo damage, and a grove of trees were knocked down nearby.

A swath of scattered tree, power line, and structural damage across central and southern Jefferson County. This included many uprooted and snapped trees, power lines down, and fallen trees on homes and vehicles especially in Fort Atkinson and Jefferson. The entire roof of a home was removed by the strong winds in Jefferson near the high school. Lakeview Cemetery in Fort Atkinson suffered significant tree damage with trees down on grave sites. An agricultural business near Hellenville sustained damage to fences and shelters built for animals. A 60 mph wind was estimated at the National Weather Service office several miles southeast of Sullivan.

A swath of scattered tree and powerline damage across the county, but with heavier concentrations of damage in some areas. There was widespread tree damage on the west side of Lake Okauchee, and also a concentration of uprooted and snapped trees, including some felled on homes, near North Prairie. Another concentration of many snapped pine trees near the intersection of Waterville Rd. and Robinhood Dr. Another concentration of trees and powerlines down near Big Bend and yet another in the Sussex area.
Timmerman Airport AWOS measured a 61 mph wind gust.
A large tree down on cars at the intersection of 20th St. and West Greenfield Ave.
Multiple social media reports of tree limbs and trees down in northern and western Milwaukee.
Multiple social media reports of trees and tree limbs down in southwest Milwaukee.
Several large tree downs. Another tree down on County Highway L just to the south.
A couple trees down on the north side of Whitewater.
Some siding damage.
A total of six trees down across the county and one tree down on a powerline.
A barn collapsed while being occupied by 30 to 40 cattle. Some deceased cattle reported.
Dozens of trees uprooted or snapped.

Widespread reports of tree and powerline damage across the county. A barn 3 miles north of Lowell had the north wall blown in, while the barn door in the south end was torn off and blown into a field. There was a greater concentration of uprooted and snapped trees southeast of Neosho and near Ashippun, extending to the Washington County line. Some structural damage reported to small buildings.
Many trees and some small building damage from Erin toward the Dodge County line.
The total loss of a small shed and a Tobacco Shed to a fire was attributed to a lightning strike.
Some trees uprooted and snapped.
A 100 year old barn collapsed.

Measured wind gust of 77 mph at General Mitchell International Airport. The city of Milwaukee received more than 200 calls for downed trees and branches. Many reports of trees landing on homes, vehicles, and roads. Similar reports also in the suburbs of Milwaukee County. More than 50 percent of the roof torn off a warehouse building in the Port of Milwaukee.  Approximately 51,000 We Energies customers were without power due to downed powerlines.
A creek overflowing and some yard and basement flooding.
Flash flooding of streets in Watertown. A few stranded vehicles across the city.  A 3 to 4 foot sinkhole occurred due to the floodwaters.
Flash flooding of streets from Sussex toward Menomonee Falls.
Some street flooding in Germantown.

Flash flooding of streets in southern Ozaukee County. More specifically, flooded roads and intersections on Mequon Rd. from Wauwatosa Rd. to just east of I-43. Other intersections  across the area with 3-6 inches of standing water.

Flash flooding of streets and sidewalks mainly in northwest Milwaukee County, including stranded vehicles in floodwaters. Some reports of basement flooding in northern Milwaukee County. Pictures and videos provided.

Loveland Road closed after a washout from the flooding of Ore Creek. In the southern portion of the county, brief portions of Peters Rd, Hillside Rd. near Mohawk Rd., and Fellows Rd. just north of County Highway B were briefly closed due to flooding, but no road damage.
Floodwaters over a portion of highway 140 on the north side of Clinton.
A barn wall was blown down.
An uprooted tree.
Total destruction of a greenhouse and damage to other outbuildings. Multiple trees uprooted and leaning to the north northeast.
Flash flooding of creeks flowing over several rural roads. This included a flooded road in Cobb, floodwaters over bridges on Amacher Hollow Rd. and Sawle Rd.
Flash flooding of creeks leading to flooded roads at the intersection of County Highway F and FF, and State Highway 104 north of Brodhead.
Flooding of Butler Creek flowing over a bridge on County Highway N.

Around 700 911 calls mainly attributed to flash flooding. Flash flooding of streets and yards in Janesville with basement flooding in many homes. Many vehicles stranded in deep water. A bridge was washed out due to the flooding of Fisher Creek over Rockport Rd. Severe flooding of a church, and the basement of an elementary school. The school's mechanical systems and main power panel were destroyed. The school has been closed. RAJ stadium flooded. A train derailment in downtown Janesville with 3  locomotives off the tracks, due to a sinkhole. 1st responders conducted a water rescue of the engineer using a rope.
Numerous social media videos depicting street flooding throughout the county.
Flash flooding of streets from the 1600 to 1700 block of 2 Mile Rd. Flash flooding at the 1000 block of 61st Dr.  Flooding at 67th Dr. and Mill Ave. Flash flooding at Sharp Rd. and Rowntree Rd.
A few areas of fallen and split trees in Lake Geneva.
Pictures provided.
Pictures provided by the weather observer at Mitchell Field.
Lightning struck and killed a boy watching the storms outside. He lived on Ebenezer Road in the Civil Town of Watertown.

Although this heavy rain event was assigned to Kenosha County, heavy rain did affect part of the following counties in Southcentral or Southeast Wisconsin: Jefferson, Waukesha, Milwaukee, Rock, Walworth, and Racine.  Ponding of water on roads and in other low spots was reported in many locations.  Rainfall amounts include: 3.14 at the Kenosha Waste Water Treatment Plant (Kenosha Co.), 2.96 in Delavan (Walworth Co.), 2.82 in Wind Point (Racine Co.), 2.56 at the Racine Waste Water Treatment Plant (Racine Co.), 2.50 in Franksville (Racine Co.), 2.20 in Lake Geneva (Walworth Co.), 1.96 at Milwaukee Mitchell Field (KMKE - Milwaukee Co.), 1.93 at 2SSE Waukesha (Waukesha Co.), 1.92 at the NWS Office about 3.8SE of Sullivan (Jeffeson Co.), 1.75  at 2SE Timmerman Field (Milwaukee Co.), and 0.94 at 5SW Madison Capitol Square (Dane Co.).

Rainfall amounts include: 3.01 at the NWS Office about 3.8SSE of Sullivan (Jefferson Co.), 2.28 at 1.2SW of Palmyra, 2.60 at Beloit College (Rock Co.), 2.48 in Pell Lake (Walworth Co.), 2.46 in Paddock Lake (Kenosha Co.), 2.37 in Waterford (Racine Co.), 2.11 at 2SE Waukesha (Waukesha Co.), and 1.81 at Milwaukee Mitchell Field (Milwaukee Co.).  Rainfall amounts tapered off to 1 to 1.25 in the Madison (Dane Co.) to Sheboygan area (Sheboygan Co.).
Powerful thunderstorm wind gusts leveled many large trees, and blew down a pole shed that had 30 cows inside.

A 30-foot tall tree was snapped and uprooted in Rock River Park, and several other trees were toppled in the area southwest and west of Ft. Atkinson.  In addition, some of the toppled trees and broken branches knocked down a couple power-lines that resulted in the loss of electrical power to 300 customers.
A couple street signs and fencing were damaged and several large trees were uprooted by powerful thunderstorm wind gusts.

events.event_narrative: A microburst generated a 100 yard wide swath of tree and structural damage from just southeast of the Village of Farmersville northeast to Knowles.  Wind gusts were estimated at 78 knots (90 mph). Damage included...2 barns down killing 7 cows, 4 sheds and 1 greenhouse destroyed, and 5 homes affected (minor damage).  Also, about 150 trees were toppled or damaged. Heavy rainfall between 1.50 inches and 2.60 inches caused ponding of water on roads in the area.

This event is a continuation of a swath of thunderstorm wind damage that affected northeast Rock County and northwest Walworth County.  Many large trees were damaged or uprooted in southeast Jefferson County. The swath was about 4 miles wide.

A swath of thunderstorm wind damage raked northeast Rock County.  Many large trees were uprooted or damaged.  The swath was about 4 miles wide.  This event continued into northwest Walworth County and then southeast Jefferson County.
Several large trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds in Waterford.
Several large trees were blown down in the downtown area.
Many reports of toppled trees and damaged power-lines were received from within and near Dodgeville to a couple miles east of Mineral Point.
Hail increased from 1.75 at 22:23 to 2.75 at 22:25.

Heavy rainfalls of 1 to 3 inches (estimate based on radar and reports) in the Madison to Sun Prairie area resulted in flash flooding.  Many streets and roads were flooded to a depth of 1 to 3 feet.  Several gravel shoulder washouts were reported.
An entire grove of trees was toppled.
Several large trees were blown down from thunderstorm winds.  One road was blocked by tree debris.
A few large trees were toppled and power-line were down due to tree debris.
Several large trees were toppled and a couple power-lines sustained damage due to tree debris.

Numerous reports of flash flooding were received from the Waukesha to Brookfield and New Berlin areas.  A couple gravel shoulder washouts were reported, and some minor damage to basement contents occurred.  Water depths on roads reached 1 to 3 feet.  A water control facility in New Berlin was damaged by flood waters ($100K).

Numerous reports of flash flooding were received from the West Allis, Wauwatosa, Milwaukee, and Greenfield areas.  Several roads were flooded to a depth of 1 to 3 feet, and there was standing water on I-894 in Greenfield.  West Allis received 3.68 of rain in 1 hour around the midnight hour.  A couple cars sustained water damage.
Seveal large trees were toppled and a couple power-lines down sustained damage due to tree debris.  A tree fell on a car.
