A trained storm spotter witnessed a brief EF0 tornado that touched down about 2.7 miles northeast of Herman Center in Dodge County, just north of the intersection of County Road DW and Freedom Road. The tornado traveled less than one-tenth of a mile before dissipating. The maximum path width of the tornado was 20 yards with an average path width of 10 yards. The spotter noted small tree limbs snapped off, and tall grass flattened in a swirl pattern by the winds from the tornado. The EF0 rating was determined by using DI 27(TH), DOD1 with winds of 65 mph. The exact location  was 43.4497/ -88.44074.
Several large trees were uprooted by powerful thunderstorm winds.

Dozens of large trees were uprooted by powerful thunderstorm winds and broken tree branches in a 3-mile wide swath from 3 miles southeast of Dayton to the Albany area.  Near the intersection of STH 59 and CTH F, a barn, built in the 1940s, was pushed over by the winds.  A hanger at the Albany Airport on STH 59 was damaged by the winds.  A few miles north-northwest of Albany the winds damaged some siding and the roof of a barn.
The City of Cudahy Emergency Manager reported numerous trees down in the city. One tree severely damaged a mobile home-trailer.

Law enforcement officials reported numerous trees and power lines down across far eastern Racine County from severe thunderstorm winds that gusted up to 82 mph (71 knots) measured by the ASOS at Racine Batten Airport. A C-130 cargo airplane parked at the airport was spun 40-50 degrees and moved 31 feet by the severe wind gusts. Many large branches were also broken off by the powerful winds, which also blew shingles off of several homes. The thunderstorm outflow winds caused roof damage to a house and garage in the 4800 block of State Highway 31.

Law enforcement officials reported numerous trees and power lines down across far eastern Kenosha County from severe thunderstorm winds that gusted up to 75 mph (65 knots) as estimated by a trained spotter.  A 31-year-old man riding a motorcycle was killed when a tree blew over on him in the 7600 block of 25th Avenue. A Pleasant Prairie woman injured her hip when she was struck by debris form a shed. Two other residents of the City of Kenosha were injured when they touched live wires brought down by the strong winds. Many large branches were also broken off by the powerful winds, which also damaged several homes. Officials estimate 500 to 800 trees were destroyed or badly damaged by the winds.

This EF1 tornado touched down about 4.4 miles west-southwest of the town of Alto in Fond Du Lac County, on Marshview Road, about one-third of a mile north of Lake Maria Road, and tracked about 2.6 miles to the north-northwest before crossing into Green Lake County, about 3.7 miles south-southwest of Fairwater, at County Road S approximately 1/4 mile east of Schure Road. This tornado exhibited three separate damage tracks within the path, suggesting three separate vortices formed and dissipated during the life span of the tornado. The average path width was 75 yards, with a maximum path width of 105 yards. The tornado blew over trees and flattened a pole shed. The EF1 rating was determined by using DI 21(MBS) DOD5 LB to EXP with estimated winds speeds of 105 mph. The exact starting point was 43.77112/-88.88480 and the exact ending point was 43.78370/-88.88558.

This EF1 tornado crossed into Green Lake County from Fond Du Lac County, about 4.9 miles east-southeast of Markesan, at County Road S approximately 1/4 mile east of Schure Road, and traveled a little over 2 miles to the north-northwest before dissipating approximately 3.7 miles east of Markesan, about 1200 feet northwest of the intersection of Utley Road and County Trunk Highway Q. The average path width was 75 yards, with a maximum path width of 105 yards. The tornado blew over trees and blew a door and a side panel off a pole shed. Roof shingles were also blown off of several buildings, with one home having minor roof, gutter and awning damage. The EF1 rating was determined by using DI 27(TH) DOD4 LB toward EXP with estimated winds speeds of 100 mph. The exact starting point was 43.78370/-88.88558 and the exact ending point was 43.79798/-88.91194.

This EF1 tornado touched down approximately 2.3 miles of northwest of Fairwater, about 200 feet southeast of the intersection of Watson Road and Searl Road/County Line Road, and traveled nearly parallel to County Line Road for almost a mile to the north-northwest before crossing County Line Road about 2000 feet north of Carter Road into Green Lake County.  The average path width was 60 yards, with a maximum path width of 100 yards. The tornado uprooted trees and tore away a wall and part of the roof of a barn. The EF1 rating was determined by using DI 1(SBO) DOD4 EXP toward UB with estimated winds speeds of 95 mph. The exact starting point was 43.66761/-88.86583 and the exact ending point was 43.70275/-88.88517.

This EF1 tornado entered into Green Lake County from Fond Du Lac County at Searl Road/ County Line Road about 2000 feet north of Carter Road into Green Lake County.  The average path width was 60 yards, with a maximum path width of 100 yards. The tornado uprooted trees and tore away metal panels off the roof of a pole shed. Officials reported up to 40 large trees uprooted, and numerous branches broken by powerful thunderstorm winds.

A 2-mile wide swath of damage was caused by a microburst associated with a bowing line of severe thunderstorms that tracked from southwest to northeast across a large portion of Waukesha County. Wind gusts estimated up to between 100 to 110 mph (87 to 96 knots) dropped thousands of trees, damaged homes and barns and blew down power lines that left 10,000 customers without power in Waukesha County. One person was injured by airborne tree debris near the Pewaukee and Delafield town borders. A semi-trailer truck was blown over on Interstate-94 in Waukesha County, while two other high-profile vehicles were nearly blown over by the strong winds, but concrete construction barriers saved the vehicles from being completely blown over.

Part of a line of severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts up to 70 mph (60 knots) that blew down numerous trees moved through northeast and eastern Waukesha County during the middle afternoon of June 21st.

Part of a line of severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts estimated up to 64 mph (56 knots) that blew down numerous trees and power lines moved through southern Washington County during the middle afternoon of June 21st. The powerful wind gusts blew a tree down on a house and knocked down a barn near Holy Hill.

A trained spotter reported large hail, estimated to be 1.25 inches in diameter, that fell near a Y.M.C.A. camp east of Burlington.

Heavy downpours of rain, associated with a line of strong to severe thunderstorms that crossed southern Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours of June 21st, dropped between 1.5 inches and 2 inches of rain over a 1 hour to a 1 1/2 hour time period. The heavy rain caused flash flooding that covered some roads with 1 to 2 feet of water. One lane of Highway 100 in Franklin was closed due to the high water, with a vehicle stalled in water on National Avenue and the Root River Parkway in West Allis.

Heavy downpours of rain, associated with a line of strong to severe thunderstorms that crossed southern Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours of June 21st, dropped between 1.5 inches and 2 inches of rain over a 1 to 2 hour time period. Law enforcement officials reported the intersection of Lily Road and Burleigh Road in Brookfield, was closed, as were many other roads in the surrounding area, due to the high water covering the roadways. In Jefferson, three buildings were damaged: one of them had extensive damage to its roof and interior ceilings, a business's outdoor sign was damaged, and motel had a roof peel and several imploded windows.  A fence in a subdivision east of Cambridge was blown down.  A few roads were temporarily closed until tree debris was removed.

Circuit breakers in the home were blown out, and the telephone pedestal box outside the home was blown to the other side of the road.

The roof of the other shed was lifted from it's foundation, damaging electrical utilities attached to it and adjacent buildings before settling back down. Law enforcement officials, as well as many members of the general public, reported a tornado that formed and stayed over Lake Monona, about 1 mile east of Law Park in the City of Madison.  The tornado tracked south, then southeast, over the lake before dissipating west of Squaw Bay, about 1/4 mile north of Waunona Park.  No damage was reported.  The tornado kicked up water spray, estimated about 20 feet wide at the surface of the water expanding to 40 feet wide about 40 feet above the water.  Many public reports of the tornado/waterspout came into local law enforcement, along with photos and video clips of the vortex from a variety of locations around the lake.  The associated condensation funnel never developed more than half-way down to the water surface.  Though actually a waterspout, it is being termed a tornado in the official Storm Data report due to National Weather Service rules that limit waterspout reports to bodies of water with a designated marine zone.  Lake Monona does not have an assigned marine zone number.  The exact starting point was Lat 43.06722 and Lon -89.36588, the mid-point was Lat 43.05864 and Lon -89.36147, and the end point was Lat 43.05263 and Lon -89.35266.  The average path width was 15 yards.  This tornado-waterspout had estimated wind speeds of 30 to 40 mph based on eyewitness reports.  This value is below the minimum wind speed of an EF-0 tornado which is 65 mph in the current EF-Scale.

Severe thunderstorms with strong wind gusts produced damage across Marquette County, including a 10-mile wide swath of damage from west of Westfield to Germania. The damaging winds downed power lines and trees, including a tree that crushed a parked car on CTH B in Montello. Five homes received minor damage to roofs, siding and gutters due to tree debris striking the homes. At the peak of the storm, 937 homes were without electricity. A mesonet site one mile north of Westfield recorded a 67 mph (58 knot) wind gust.

Severe thunderstorms with strong wind gusts produced damage across central Fond Du Lac County. The damaging winds downed power lines and trees, knocking out power to businesses and homes on the west side of the city of Fond Du Lac.

The Iowa County Emergency manager reported damage from severe thunderstorm wind gusts estimated at 70 knots (80 mph) in a 5-mile wide swath from south of Linden to south-southwest of Dodgeville. The damaging winds blew the roof off of a cattle barn south of Dodgeville and knocked over a grain bin. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down by the powerful winds.

Law enforcement officials reported damage from severe thunderstorm wind gusts estimated at 70 knots (80 mph) in a 5-mile wide swath from southeast of Dodgeville to northeast of Hollandale. The damaging winds destroyed a cattle shed and caused minor damage to a barn. The winds damaged several corn fields on East Lawinger Road southeast of Dodgeville. A grain bin was knocked off its foundation and destroyed, and a corn field was flattened northeast of Hollandale. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down by the powerful winds.

Law enforcement officials reported damage from severe thunderstorm wind gusts estimated at 65 knots (75 mph) in a 4-mile wide swath from north of Portland to north of Ashippun. The damaging winds downed numerous trees and power lines.

Fire officials had the gas line problem resolved by 4:30 pm CDT (3:30 pm CST).

Heavy rains resulted in flash flooding of a construction zone on the west frontage road of I-94 between STH 20 and CTH C.  A 76-year-old Dousman man died when his car stalled in the flood waters after driving into a flooded ditch in the construction zone.  The preliminary cause of death was from a heart attack and hypothermia, suffered when the victim apparently tried to leave the marooned car and walk for help. His body was found in the flood water about 100 yards from his car.

Strong and gusty northwest winds developed over South-Central Wisconsin behind a cold front trailing from rapidly strengthening low pressure that tracked across northern Wisconsin into northern Lower Michigan on Thursday, September 29th. The resulting tight pressure gradient over the state during the late afternoon of the 29th produced a peak wind gust of 68 mph (59 knots) recorded 1 mile south of Monroe by a trained spotter.  Sustained surface winds up to 43 mph (37 knots) and surface wind gusts up to 55 mph (48 knots) were measured by the AWOS at the Monroe Airport. The strong winds toppled trees and downed power lines across Green County.

Strong winds broke off tree limbs and knocked down power lines across Milwaukee County with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph, and peak wind gusts up to 45 mph. The power outages resulted indirectly to the death of a 49-year-old man with muscular dystrophy who was dependent on a ventilator. Backup batteries that powered the ventilator during the outage gave out before the man could get emergency medical care.

A weak rain-wrapped tornado spun up 2.17 miles north-northeast of Arlington northwest of the intersection of Krier Rd. and Thiele Ed and moved northeast for about 3.5 miles before dissipating midway between King Road and Mud Lake just southwest of Mud Lake.  The ending location would be 4 miles east of Poynette.  This tornado crossed STH 22 at the intersection of Loveland Road and then curved more north-northeast and tracked about 300 yards just east of the intersection of STH 22 and CTH CS.  Several outbuildings were damaged and a 3000 lb farm implement was tossed about 500 feet.  Due to wet soils, two power-poles were partially tipped over.  A couple vehicles were damaged and other farm equipment scattered around. One home sustained minor siding and roof shingle damage.  Otherwise, the usual tree damage occurred and a couple trees were uprooted.  The corn crop was only a few inches in height but some stalks were broken off at ground level.  Tree damage was consistent with DI 27 Hardwood Trees (TH) and DOD3 which suggests wind speeds of 90 to 95 mph.  The path length was about 3.7 miles and maximum width was 125 yards.  The average width was about 50 yards.

The Iowa County Emergency Manager reported numerous trees and power lines blown down by thunderstorm wind gusts estimated at 64 mph (56 knots).

The Columbia County 911 Call Center reported approximately 100 trees were blown down, many power lines downed and scattered clusters of damage along a 17 mile-wide path from 5 miles southwest of Portage to Columbus from damaging thunderstorm wind gusts that were estimated up to 80 mph. Heavy rain accompanying the storms, with 1.58 inches measured in 45 minutes 3 miles east of Poynette, produced street flooding in Portage and Pardeeville.

The river gauge on the Fox River at New Munster remained above flood stage from the afternoon of June 25th into July. The river experienced minor flooding, cresting at 12.79 feet at 1030 AM CDT on June 28th, which is 2.79 feet above flood stage.

The river gauge on the Pecatonica River near Blanchardville remained above flood stage from the morning of June 22nd to the evening of June 27th. The river experienced moderate flooding, cresting at 14.33 feet at 4 PM CDT on June 23rd, which is 3.33 feet above flood stage.

The river gauge on Turtle Creek in Beloit remained above flood stage from the morning of June 25th to the morning of June 28th. The creek experienced moderate flooding, cresting at 13.95 feet at 4:50 AM CDT on June 27th, which is 4.95 feet above flood stage.

The river gauge on Turtle Creek near Clinton remained above flood stage from the morning of June 25th to the late afternoon of June 27th. The creek experienced moderate flooding, cresting at 11.76 feet at 4:15 PM CDT on June 26th, which is 3.76 feet above flood stage.

The river gauge on the Sugar River in Brodhead remained above flood stage from the afternoon of June 24th into early July. The creek experienced moderate flooding, cresting at 8.86 feet at 2:00 AM CDT on June 28th, which is 3.86 feet above flood stage.

The river gauge on the Yahara River near Fulton remained above flood stage from the morning of June 26th to the early morning of June 27th. The river experienced major flooding, cresting at 12.06 feet at 3:30 PM CDT on June 26th, which is 2.06 feet above flood stage.

The river gauge on the Pecatonica River near Martintown remained above flood stage from the morning of June 25th into early July. The river experienced minor flooding, cresting at 15.56 feet at 10:15 AM CDT on June 28th, which is 2.06 feet above flood stage.

events.cz_name: WIND PT LT WI TO WINTHROP HBR IL
events.event_narrative: Multiple pictures and videos of this waterspout were viewed.  Kenosha Police recorded a video of this waterspout and waterspout #2 from Southport Park in southern Kenosha. This waterspout did not affect any watercraft.

events.cz_name: WIND PT LT WI TO WINTHROP HBR IL
events.event_narrative: Multiple video and photographs from Law Enforcement and the general public show waterspout #2 developing just east of waterspout #1 and moving south to southeast in the near shore waters.  Waterspout #2 did not affect any watercraft.

events.cz_name: WIND PT LT WI TO WINTHROP HBR IL
events.event_narrative: General public took photographs and video of waterspout #3 developing just west of waterspout #2 and moving east to southeast further into Lake Michigan, away from the lakeshore.  No watercraft were affected by this waterspout.

events.cz_name: WIND PT LT WI TO WINTHROP HBR IL
events.event_narrative: Waterspout #4 in the series filmed by the general public.  Waterspout #4 developed very close to waterspout #3 and tracked east to southeast.  Waterspout did not affect water craft.

Tornado began near the intersection of County Highway P and State Highway 23 just west of the I-39 interchange about 1.2 miles southwest of Endeavor. The tornado moved north along a 1.78 mile long path ending just under 1 mile northwest of Endeavor about 1/2 mile north of Gail Avenue. The maximum path width was 50 yards. Trees were snapped along the path, with one tree falling on a house and car, destroying the car and damaging the roof of the house. Other homes had shingle damage with a section of metal roof peeled off of a farm house. The wind damage was consistent with an EF-0 tornado with winds of 70 to 85 mph.

She would have fallen anytime from the evening of January 2nd to the morning of January 3rd.  Her home was located near Lawrence Lake, just west of Westfield.

High winds out of the northwest were a factor in a multi-vehicle accident that killed a 86 year old man near the intersection of Highway 11 and Dunbar Road in the Town of Plymouth. The car driven by the 86 year old man crossed the center-line going westbound and collided with an eastbound Freightliner. Wind gusts were as high as 46 mph at the Janesville airport and the strong winds may have pushed the car across the center-line.

Numerous roads were closed over southern Sauk County due to flash flooding of small creeks and streams. Estimated rainfall amounts ranged from 4-7 inches. Some of the known creeks that flooded were Otter Creek, Honey Creek, North Branch of Honey Creek, and Pine Creek. There was one bridge washout at the north end of Stones Pocket Road due to the flooding of Otter Creek. This will cost approximately $150,000 to replace.

A 60 foot by 120 foot pole barn was mostly leveled. The steel sheeting from the barn was blown about 1/4 mile to the northeast. The collapse of the pole barn damaged tractors, a combine, and other farm equipment. Another farm lost roofs from two sheds and several large trees were downed with a fallen tree totaling a car. At yet another residence, fallen trees damaged two buildings. Finally another residence had a 16 inch spruce tree snapped off at the base and it partially landed on the home damaging the sofitts and gutters.
Street and parking low flooding led to water rushing into a business on highway 23 just east of Ripon. One hour rainfall estimated by doppler radar was 1.50 inches.
Multiple branches and a few trees down. The side was blown off of a new home under construction.

A large oak tree uprooted and landed on a tent killing a 10 year old girl and injuring her father and brother.  The tree fell approximately 1 hour after thunderstorms with heavy rains. Nearby observations and Doppler radar suggest around 1.90 inches of rain fell. The roots of the tree grew over a large rock and the soil was saturated from the heavy rain. These factors may have weakened the stability of the tree and it fell.
An estimated one inch of rain in 20 minutes resulted in urban street flooding with some street closures.

A 3.6 mile west to east path of significant straight line wind damage. The most concentrated damage was just south of highway 50 and east of Green Bay Road. Numerous large trees snapped and uprooted. Shingle damage to approximately 8 homes with two roofs likely requiring replacement. Many privacy fences destroyed. A large tree fell on a home. The Burger King sign was destroyed. A camper was overturned.
Water waist to chest deep near Warner Park including the 1500 block of Trailsway Drive. A vehicle was stuck in deep water in the intersection of Aberg and Huxley streets.

Many streets impassable in downtown Madison and the near east side of the city due to deep water with multiple vehicles being swept away or pushed into oncoming traffic. Some roads were closed, and manhole covers were removed by the rushing water from underneath. The eastbound beltline highway off-ramp to John Nolen Drive was closed due to deep water. The northbound side of South Park street intersecting with Wingra Drive was flooded. Some buildings were flooded near the Capital building.
Numerous streets are flooded in the city of Beloit with rainfall rates of 2-3 inches per hour.

The Milwaukee County Medical Examiner reported the death of a woman from hypothermia during the morning. She was found in the driveway of her home. The Medical Examiner also determined she was intoxicated. Temperatures throughout Sunday morning were in the upper teens Fahrenheit with wind chill temperatures around zero.

An ice jam caused the Wisconsin River at Portage to rise above flood stage at 17.08 feet for a brief period. Minor lowland flooding was already occurring from late November and continued well into December. This caused flooding of the lower roads in the Blackhawk Park area, which is between the Wisconsin River and Long Lake. The roads were closed with a few feet of water and ice on the roads. The water and ice is very near to several small homes with a small number of people having to canoe or walk to dry land.
An icy roadway from freezing drizzle led to a fatal car accident around 5:45 am in the Town of Leeds. The man was killed when his car slid into an oncoming pickup truck.

A homeless man was found deceased in an alcove near a liquor store. The Milwaukee County Medical Examiner's office determined hypothermia as the cause of death. Intoxication was another significant condition in his death. Temperatures ranged from 15-30 degrees throughout the calendar day.

Heavy rainfall of 2 to 2.25 inches in approximately one hour resulted in urban flooding in Baraboo and West Baraboo. The flooding problems were more focused in West Baraboo within construction zones that had temporary culverts in place. Some street closures were needed in these areas, which included South Boulevard near the Army National Guard, Casey's General Store, and at the roundabout near Campbell Park. Knee deep water and a few stalled cars were reported. There was some flooding in the restaurants of Culver's, Taco Bell, and resident basements.

The Wisconsin River near Portage reached moderate flood stage, eventually cresting at 18.44 feet during the evening of February 26th. Widespread flooding of the Blackhawk Park and Long Lake areas occurred with many flooded roads and road closures in that area.  Some seasonal homes along Old River Road were surrounded by floodwaters.  Farther south in the Town of Dekorra, a few homes had floodwaters in the first floor along with the flooding of outbuildings.  Floodwaters also flowed over County Highway V and River Oaks Road in the Town of Dekorra. Some residents had to use canoes or boats for transportation to and from their homes. On the west side of Portage and north of the river, floodwaters affected River Shores Rd.

Stranded vehicles with water up to the windows were reported along with several buildings and homes flooded.

A school bus rolled over into a steep ditch on highway 60 while negotiating a sharp curve in dense fog. This occurred near the intersection of highway 60 and highway 51 in Leeds Township. The driver was the only occupant. Another accident occurred in dense fog at the intersection of highway 51 and Goose Pond Road in the Arlington Township. A semi-truck collided with a car. The semi-truck driver was then hit by a car as he warned oncoming traffic of the accident.  He sustained serious injuries.

Roads closed due to flash flooding after a few inches of rain. The main roads that were closed included Redford Blvd. at I-94, the intersection of Redford Blvd. and Watertown Road, Pewaukee Road at I-94. Also in Hartland, the intersections of Lindenwood Ave. and Maple Ave., Maple Ave. and North Shore Dr., and Cottonwood Ave. and Lindenwood Ave.

A portion of the Zoo interchange from I-94 WB to I-41 NB was closed due to flooding. Also the 84th street on-ramp was closed due to high water.

Various road closures over the eastern half of Walworth County due to the flash flooding of creeks or the pooling of water in low spots after 3.50-8.00 inches of rain. Walworth County declared an emergency. Road closures near Springfield, Abells Corners, south and east of East Troy. Also, widespread flooding and road closures in and around Elkhorn after 3.26 inches of rain in an hour. The water flowed into some businesses and the Huber Dorm. Some cars were stranded in deep water.  Residents of the Bud Motors Trailer Park in the Town of Lyons evacuated due to flooding from the White River. Also in Lyons, the Ore Creek flooded and destroyed a portion of the foundation of a home. Ten additional homes were flooded and there were extensive roadway washouts in the area.

Various road closures over the eastern half of Walworth County continued due to flooding from 3.50-8.00 inches of rain. Road closures continued near Springfield, Abells Corners, south and east of East Troy. Also, road closures in and around Elkhorn and flooding continued in the Town of Lyons near the White River and Ore Creek.

Four to eight inches of rain fell over the southwest half of the county over several hours causing urban and rural flash flooding. Racine County and the city and town of Burlington declared emergencies. Many creeks flooded; thereby flooding and washing-out many roads. Some of the roads that were closed were portions of highways 11 and 20 near the communities of Kansasville and Beaumont. The Hoosier Creek flooded and washed-out a portion of Mount Tom Rd. and flooded a portion of highway J. Urban flash flooding in Burlington and Union Grove closed many roads. The Fox River began to flood with sandbagging along the river in Waterford and Burlington.

The Fox River crested in Burlington at a record level of 16.15 feet on July 13th after 4-8 inches of rain in the Fox River Basin. The city of Burlington is divided in half at this river stage from east to west. Bridges and streets in downtown Burlington are blocked off and closed, including Bridge Street. Floodwaters affect homes on the following streets north of E. Jefferson St. in Burlington: North Spring St., North Main St., East Washington St., North Wisconsin St., and Capital Street. Riverside Park and Veterans Park is flooded. Floodwaters affect a portion of Brever Road 4 miles south of Burlington. Floodwaters also approach highway 83. Various road closures over the southwest half of Racine County continued due to flooding. The power was out for much of Burlington for a few days.

Three to eight inches of rain fell over Kenosha County over several hours causing urban and rural flash flooding. The highest amounts occurred west of I-94. Kenosha County declared an emergency. Sheriff deputies assisted with the evacuations of campers at Sunrise and Sunset Campgrounds at the Richard Bong State Recreation Area. Eight people were evacuated from the Pleasant Prairie Mobile Home Park in the Town of Somers due to flooding from the Kilbourn Road Ditch. Some water rescues occurred due to vehicles driving into deep water. The Chicago-Milwaukee Amtrak Hiawatha Service and the Metra Train Service in the Milwaukee district was temporary closed due to flooding. The right lane of I-94 southbound was closed at County Highway A. Many roads were closed or washed-out in and near the Village of Paddock Lake, the Village of Salem Lakes, and in the Town of Somers. Flooding began on the Fox River in the western portion of the county.

Three to eight inches of rain fell over Kenosha County from late evening on July 11th through much of the morning of July 12th causing days of areal flooding over portions of the county, including near the Fox River.  The Fox River near New Munster had a record crest of 17.47 feet on July 13th. There was widespread flooding adjacent to the river in the Town of Wheatland, the Town of Salem, and the Village of Salem Lakes. Floodwaters are into the lower levels of some homes in those areas...including Shorewood Drive and Riverside Drive in the Village of Salem Lakes. Highway 50 is closed at the Fox River. Many roads were closed or washed-out in and near the Village of Paddock Lake, the Village of Salem Lakes, and in the Town of Somers. Wake low wind damage especially in the communities of Mount Horeb, Verona, Mt. Vernon, and the southwest side of Madison. Significant tree damage occurred. There was minor structural damage to homes in Mount Horeb due to trees landing on them or shingles being removed from high winds.

Wake low wind gusts downing tree branches.

Washouts of mainly gravel roads and driveways in the northwest portion of the county. About 50 homes with mostly minor water damage. However, the north foundation of a home collapsed while the east and west foundations buckled due to water pressure. Water was briefly over a bridge on Sunny Road at the Dodge Branch of the Pecatonica River. The flooding also led to the loss of crops.

The west branch of the Little Sugar River and the Little Sugar River flooded during the afternoon of July 20th after several inches of overnight rain. A small number of roads near the river were closed and the parking lot for the Badger and Sugar River Bike Trails was flooded. In downtown Monticello, basement flooding occurred at a cafe, the village hall, and a chemical LLC. A portion of Fahey Road, south of Belleville, was washed out during the morning hours.

Flash flooding of creeks and the Galena River in the far southwest portion of the county due to approximately 5 inches of rain. Roads, bridges, and culverts washed-out. Approximately 13 homes experienced very minor flooding with 2 homes with more substantial basement flooding.

The Baraboo River crested at 19.85 ft. which is minor flood stage. Floodwaters affect a trailer rental business and a road wayside park about 5 miles downstream from the gauge near the Highway 33 bridge. Also, water affects an auto auction business near Highway I-94.

The Baraboo River at Rock Springs crested at 16.0 ft. which is moderate flood stage. Floodwaters affected Highways DD, 154 and 136 in Rock Springs as well as Busser Park along Highway 136. Water is about 3 feet deep in the baseball diamond in Fireman's Park along Highway DD. Floodwaters affect some businesses, including the Post Office, on Highway 154 in Rock Springs.

The Baraboo River at Reedsburg crested at 16 ft. which is moderate flood stage. There is widespread inundation of lowland in the Reedsburg area at this level. Floodwaters affect West Second Street, Granite Avenue and South Webb Avenue along the river. Water affects the concrete deck of the South Webb Avenue bridge. Floodwaters are into Webb Park and Smith Conservancy. The Public Works Yard is under 2 to 2.5 feet of water.

The Pecatonica River near Blanchardville crested at 14.89 ft. which is moderate flood stage. McKellar Park in Blanchardville is completely flooded including the swimming pool and tennis courts. Floodwaters cover a portion of Highway H.

The Pecatonica River near Darlington crested at 15.35 ft. which is moderate flood stage. There is flooding in Calamine, Wisconsin, about 5 miles upstream of Darlington. Highways 23 and 81 are flooded and closed in Darlington as is a good part of Main Street. This includes the highway 23 bridge. The Lafayette County Fairgrounds are flooded.

The Pecatonica River in Martintown crested at 18.45 ft. which is moderate flood stage. Some homes in the Martintown area have floodwaters in their basements and first floors. In total, 8 homes had either very minor or minor flood damage, with 3 homes having major flood damage. One business in Browntown suffered major flood damage. Portions of Martintown Road, West River Road, and Babler Road are flooded. A portion of Zimmerman Lane was washed out. Upstream in Browntown, Highway MM and West Indies Road are flooded.
The Sugar River at Albany crested at 12.04 ft., which is minor flood stage. Floodwaters affect the village park in Albany. Floodwaters cover Tin Can Road about 2 miles northwest of Albany.

The Sugar River at Brodhead crested at 8.72 ft., which is moderate flood stage. There is widespread agricultural land flooding in the Brodhead area. Some roads are either closed or experience minor flooding, including Ten Eyck Rd. Downstream, floodwaters are over County Road T which is the border of Green and Rock County.
The Sugar River flooded from Green County into Rock County. The Avon Bottoms State Natural Area is flooded including County Road T which is the border of Green and Rock County.

Several large trees uprooted or snapped. Large branches also down. Structural damage to several homes from trees landing on them. Two pontoon boats that were resting on boat lifts were overturned into the lake.

An EF0 tornado started near the intersection of S. First St. and Winnebago St. in Madison and tracked over 9 miles to Sun Prairie, paralleling Highway 151 for most of the path. In Madison, approximately, 200 trees were damaged or destroyed. Some of the trees landed on homes, garages, and vehicles. At least three households were displaced due to damage to their homes. The rear wall of a car wash collapsed, and the three-season porch of a home collapsed.  A roof was partially torn away from a commercial building.  Many power lines were downed with some arcing. In total, four commercial buildings and 12-18 homes sustained some damage. In Sun Prairie, near and east of the intersection of W. Main St. and O'Keeffe Ave., several traffic standards, streets signs, and construction barrels were damaged or knocked down. A truck topper was removed from a truck and a small wood shed was damaged. Several trees and branches were down, including a tree on a house.

Gusty westerly winds caused panels to fall from a high-end apartment construction site near the intersection of Prospect Ave. and Ivanhoe Place. The panels landed on a parked car, destroying its windshield. In the downtown area near the Northwestern Mutual building, three panels on the underside of the skywalk broke free and landed on a parked car.

The east branch of the Pecatonica River in Blanchardville reached major flood stage, cresting at 16.02 feet. McKellar Park was completely flooded including the swimming pool, tennis courts, and football field. Highway H in Blanchardville was flooded and closed.

The Sugar River reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 9.59 feet in Brodhead. There is widespread flooding of lowland and agricultural land in the Brodhead area. Floodwaters cover roads about 6 miles downstream into the Avon Township of Rock County.  Floodwaters are over Highway T which is on the border of Green and Rock Counties.
The Sugar River flooded from Green County into Rock County. The Avon Bottoms State Natural Area and Sugar River Park is flooded, including County Road T, which is the border of Green and Rock County.

The Fox River near New Munster reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 13.37 feet. Floodwaters are into the lower levels of some homes along Riverside Dr. and Shorewood Dr. in the Village of Salem Lakes. A portion of 77th St. in the Town of Wheatland in flooded.

The Sugar River reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 13.88 feet in Albany. Floodwaters cover a low spot on Highway EE near Albany Wildlife Area about 2 miles north of Albany. Floodwaters get into the basements of some homes along South Water Street and in the basements of a few businesses on North Water Street in downtown Albany. Floodwaters affect the back yards of a few homes along South Mill Street. Floodwaters are into Village Park.

The Pecatonica River in Martintown crested at 20.07 ft., which is moderate flood stage.|Some homes in the Martintown area have floodwaters in their basements and first floors; Martintown Road and West River Road in Martintown are flooded as is Highway 73 about 1 mile downstream in Winslow, Illinois. Highways MM and West Indies Road upstream in the Browntown area are flooded. Road damage did occur to some of the flooded roads and will require repair.

The Pecatonica River near Darlington crested at 15.30 ft., which is moderate flood stage.  Highways 23 and 81 are flooded and closed in Darlington, as is a good part of Main Street. This includes the highway 23 bridge. The Lafayette County Fairgrounds are flooded. In addition, there is flooding in Calamine, Wisconsin, about 5 miles upstream of Darlington. Also, northwest of South Wayne, portions of Sargent Rd. and Larson Rd. are closed due to high water.

The Rock River near Afton rose from 4 ft. to moderate flood stage at 11.12 ft. in a 24 hour period. The sudden surge in the river level was due to abundant runoff from heavy rain falling on a frozen ground. There may have been an ice jam that formed upstream and then released. ||Floodwaters affected Riverside Park and South River Road in Janesville, in addition to  widespread lowland and agricultural flooding in the Afton and Janesville areas. Floodwaters affected a home on South Christian Road on the east side of the river in the Afton area.

The Turtle Creek at Beloit reached moderate flood stage and crested at 11.70 feet. Floodwaters are in the back yards of some homes on Shopiere Road about 3 miles northeast of downtown Beloit, and on Arrowhead Drive and Luety Parkway. Colley Road is closed between Sager Lane and Sherwood Drive. Floodwaters surround a power substation on Colley Road in Beloit. Floodwaters are in the backyards of some homes on East Ridge Road, Moccasin Trail, and in the Turtle Creek subdivision. Parts of Bootmaker Drive and Moccasin Trail are flooded and closed.  Parts of Athletic Avenue and Hancock Streets are closed. About 7 miles northeast of Beloit in the Town of Turtle, Sweet-Allyn Park on Highway J is flooded and closed. In the Town of Tiffany about 8 miles northeast of Beloit, floodwaters are in the back yards of some homes on East Creek Road.
Spring Creek in Lodi reached major flood stage, cresting at 7.90 ft. There was widespread flooding in Goeres Park and Habermann Park, including the baseball diamond.
Widespread flooding of lowland and agricultural land including some roads. County officials sandbagged and pumped water out of areas in the Village of Arena, which saved 14 homes from flooding.

Periods of heavy rain in June led to very high water levels on the Yahara chain of lakes and surrounding marshland. Residents on the northeast side of Lake Kegonsa and on Lake Waubesa near Goodland Park were able to mitigate the effects of the high water by employing 8500 sandbags, and removing boats, boat lifts, and piers. Approximately 17 homes and their lake property, mainly on Sunnyside St. and Williams Dr. near Lake Kegonsa and the Door Creek wetland area, were protected by the mitigation efforts. Flooding from the Door Creek wetland area posed a greater risk than a record breaking level of 845.75 inches on Lake Kegonsa. Mitigation was also employed for a few homes on Lake Waubesa near Goodland Park. Only minor flooding occurred to some of the homes that were in the high water areas.

A male teenager jumped into Lake Michigan at the north pier in Kenosha Wisconsin during a period when strong winds and high waves were creating dangerous swimming conditions on Lake Michigan. The teenager disappeared under the waves due to structural and rip currents under the water. A second person also jumped into the water, but was able to climb out. The teenager's body was found 6 days later several miles north of the pier along the Lake Michigan shore near Carthage College.

Ozaukee County Emergency Manager first alerted WFO MKX about a missing swimmer at Harrington Beach State Park along the Lake Michigan shore.  A group of 5 people went swimming in dangerous swimming conditions when strong onshore winds were creating high waves and an increased risk of sub-surface currents.  Of the five swimmers, four people returned to the beach.  Of the four, a woman in her 30s suffered life-threatening injures due to water inhalation, and died.  The missing male swimmer turned up about two weeks later on September 4th at Whitefish Dunes State Park, about 120 miles north along the Lake Michigan shore.  An autopsy confirmed the male died from drowning.

Approximately 100 911 calls related to flash flooding in Watertown. Numerous streets in Watertown flooded and closed. Some neighborhoods completely flooded with streets, yards, and driveways filled with water. Basement flooding common. A portion of Jefferson Rd. washed out at the bridge where a creek flows into the nearby Rock River. Other road damage or washouts as well. Three vehicle water rescues involving 4 citizens performed by the fire department. A section of track ballast was washed away compromising the railroad ties and tracks. The flooding caused a sanitary sewer overflow/bypass around 10 AM.  Additional street flooding and basement flooding in Waterloo, Ixonia, and northern Jefferson County with some city streets and county roads closed and damaged. Overall, 93 homes sustained affected damage and 66 homes with minor damage. 5 businesses also sustained minor damage.

Approximately 100 911 calls related to flash flooding in Watertown. Numerous streets in Watertown flooded and closed. Some neighborhoods completely flooded with streets, yards, and driveways filled with water. Basement flooding common. Three vehicle water rescues involving 4 citizens performed by the fire department. Railroad tracks compromised by soil erosion underneath the tracks.  The flooding caused a sanitary sewer overflow/bypass around 10 AM. Lowland flooding in rural areas of far southern Dodge County.
Flash flooding of some streets in Marshall. Schlimgen Rd. near the Deansville State Wildlife Area was closed due to flooding.

Flooded roads, yards, fields, and basements continued the remainder of the day with some improvement after 5 to 8 inches of rain.  The cities of Watertown and Waterloo were most impacted by the flood waters. The Rock River in Watertown briefly reached minor flood stage from 11:10 AM CST to 12:00 PM CST. Lowland areas and parks near the Rock River were flooded throughout northern Jefferson County.
Flooded roads, yards, fields, and basements continued the remainder of the day with some improvement after 5 to 8 inches of rain.  The city of Watertown was most impacted by the flood waters.

Damage was noted to flags, a large tree limb and metal casing from a US Bank |sign. A small dumpster was also tipped behind the bank. The tornado then tracked to the west northwest through the Wileman Elementary School grounds where numerous large tree limbs were downed. Rubber roofing material on a portion of the school building was lifted and set back in place. The tornado then tracked through residences to the west northwest downing numerous limbs and a rotted/damaged tree. Gutter and roofing damage was noted on one home.

The widespread flash flooding of creeks and streets in Middleton, Verona, and the west side of Madison resulted in dozens of flooded or stranded vehicles, over 50 water rescues, and hundreds of citizens stranded in place. One drowning death occurred when a man attempted to escape the flood waters by exiting his vehicle. Many city streets were closed including major thoroughfares. 70 residences in the village of Shorewood Hills suffered water damage with 15 families displaced from their homes. Basement flooding was common in Madison and suburbs to the west and south. Water rescues were also executed just west of Verona on County Highway PD due to flash flooding of the Sugar River. Some rural roads south of Madison and Verona were closed due to flooding from the Sugar River or other creeks, including portions of highway 69. Flood waters at Morey Airport in Middleton tipped over a 500 gallon tank of gasoline and a 1,000 gallon tank of jet fuel. The gas tank leaked and was contained by a containment berm.
Sheboygan lakeshore weather station measured a wind gust of 45 knots as strong thunderstorms moved through.

Historic flash flooding of Black Earth Creek and various creeks and low lying areas of western Dane County caused significant flooding impacts. This included hundreds of citizens rescued, evacuated, or stranded, especially along the highway 14 corridor which parallels Black Earth Creek. Homes and businesses in Cross Plains, Black Earth, and Mazomanie were most impacted.  Approximately one half the village of Mazomanie was flooded by Black Earth Creek. 160 homes in Mazomanie were affected while 100 of them experienced water on the 1st floor of the home. 6-12 homes will likely need to be demolished. A bridge was partially washed out on highway 14 near Black Earth, with highway 14 being closed from Middleton to the Iowa County line due to many washouts and high water. Many other roads in western Dane County were closed due to washouts and high water, including southbound 151 near Mount Horeb and large portions of highway 78.  The Black Earth Creek reached record levels of 9.73 feet and 16.6 feet at Black Earth and Mazomanie respectively.

Black Earth Creek crested at 9.73 feet at Black Earth around 2:00 AM on 8/21/18, and at 16.6 feet at Mazomanie around 7:00 AM. The Sugar River and many other creeks and low lying areas continued to flood. The historic flooding resulted in hundreds of citizens rescued, evacuated, or stranded, especially along the highway 14 corridor which parallels Black Earth Creek and then continues into Middleton and Madison. Homes and businesses in Cross Plains, Black Earth, Mazomanie, Middleton, and the west side of Madison were most impacted. Overall, Dane County had 380 homes with affected damage, 857 homes with minor damage, 302 homes with major damage, and 5 homes destroyed. 27 businesses had minor damage and 17 suffered major damage. |A bridge was partially washed out on highway 14 near Black Earth, with highway 14 being closed from Middleton to the Iowa County line due to many washouts and high water. Many other roads in western Dane County were closed due to washouts and high water, including southbound 151 near Mount Horeb and large portions of highway 78. 5000 feet of railroad tracks on the Wisconsin & Southern Railroad were washed out between Mazomanie and Madison.

The Sugar River rose rapidly in Belleville and flooded Belleville Communitiy Park and some neighborhoods. Nine families were evacuated from the east side of the town. The highway 69 bridge was closed and highway 92 was closed between River St. and County Road PB due to high water from the Sugar River.

Sections of the isthmus in Madison, including many streets,  experienced sustained flooding due to record high water levels on Lake Mendota and Lake Monona. Much of the flooding was near the Yahara River which connects Lake Mendota to Lake Monona. Additional flooding occurred in lakeshore areas of Lake Mendota, Lake Monona, and Lake Waubesa. Thousands of sandbags were deployed to prevent flood damages. Streets, bike paths, parks, boat launches and piers were closed in the isthmus and other areas in the Yahara Chain of Lakes. This overall flooding continued through the end of August and into early September.

A male hunter drowned on the Fox River near the inlet to Puckaway Lake after the boat capsized due to strong winds from passing rain and snow showers. The other occupant and dog made it safely to shore.

Highway 14 was inundated and closed by flood waters just west of County Road K due to record flooding of Black Earth and Blue Mounds Creeks.

Overall, many flooded roads and lowlands due to 4 to 8 inches of rain. Some road washouts and homes flooded. I-43 was closed through late morning due to flooding between mile marker 101 and 107. Many of the cities in the county experienced severe street flooding and closures. The Milwaukee River reached minor flood stage throughout the county with many roads and intersections flooded and closed near the river, especially near Saukville and Cedarburg. Some piers washed away on the Milwaukee River. Dozens of vehicles across the county were stranded in flood waters. Overall, 76 homes sustained affected flood damage, 52 homes with minor flood damage, and 11 homes with major damage. 25 businesses sustained minor flood damage and 5 businesses sustained major flood damage.

Various roads and bridges remained closed from the prior heavy rains and flooding that had occurred. Additional roads and bridges were becoming inundated with high water from creeks and the Baraboo River in the far northwest portion of the county.

The Baraboo River also began to flood farther downstream in the Baraboo area. Other roads, bridges, and lowland areas across northern Sauk County remained flooded and closed from the heavy rains of the last several days. This tornado inflicted minor damage on 3 structures and moderate damage on 2 structures in the County of Walworth (homes/pole sheds/barn), and uprooted or damaged a couple dozen trees.  It spun up very near a drainage ditch/creek just west of West Court/Center Drive which which branches west from CTH U.  This tornado crossed into Kenosha County about 0.4 mile north of where CTH U in Walworth County crosses the county line and becomes CTH F in Walworth County.  It contiuned for several miles in western Kenosha County.  The average path width was about 50 yards in Walworth County.  The winds were estimated at 93 mph (DI 1 - SBO, DOD 5).  The specific starting location in Walworth County was 42.54884,-88.33343, and the ending location in Walworth County was 42.56342,-88.30533.  Refer to the western Kensoha County tornado event to see a map plot of the entire tornado path.

This tornado in western Kenosha County was a continuation of the tornado that spun up 2.27 mils NE of Pell Lake in southeastern Walworth County.  It crossed into Kenosha County about 0.4 mile north of where CTH U in Walworth County crosses the county line and becomes CTH F in Walworth County.  The tornado continued northeast to just east of the intersection of STH 50 and CTH O, crossed STH 83 just north of 51st Street just north of New Munster Creek, passed through the Village of Wheatland, turned more east and crossed 308th Ave. just north of Peterson Creek, and then dissipated near a pond between CTH PH and 41st Street (Town Rd).  Fifteen people in the Civil Town of Wheatland sustained minor injuries.  Also in the Civil Town of Wheatland, 7 homes were affected, 25 sustained minor damage, 27 had major damage, and 25 were destroyed.  In the Civil Town of Brighton, 10 homes were affected, 3 had minor damage, 3 had major damage, and 4 were destroyed.  About 160 people were homeless due to residential damage.  This tornado traveled over frozen ponds and creeks, as well as snow piles leftover from recent snowmelt.  Average path width was about 100 yards.  The wind speed was estimated at 150 to 160 mph (DI 2 - FR12, DOD 8).  For a couple homes, the visual damage suggested an EF4 rating, however insufficient anchoring allowed these structures to fail at a lower wind speed.  Additionally, other nearby damage indicators didn't support an EF4 rating.  The specific starting location in Kenosha County was 42.556342,-88.30533, and the ending location was 42.60061,-88.13524.  For plotting purposes, here are a couple mid-point locations of this tornadoe's path: crossing of STH 83 - 42.59297, -88.22230, and the crossing of CTH B - 42.59756, -88.15928.

This tornado was the 2nd of two tornadoes to affect southeastern Wisconsin on January 7th.  It spun up near the intersection of CTH L (18th St.) and 47th Ave. and moved east/northeast through the northern reaches of the city of Kenosha, and dissipated just north of Carthage College and just short of Lake Michigan.  In the Civil Town of Somers it resulted in minor damage to 2 homes, and major damage to one home.  In the City of Kenosha, it affected one home, inflicted minor damage to 21 homes, inflicted major damage to 6 homes, and destroyed 5 homes.  Additionally, it destroyed one church in the City of Kenosha.  Several power-lines were toppled and there were transformer explosions.  Dozens of trees were damaged or uprooted.  Average path width was about 50 yards.  The maximum winds were estimated at around 95 mph (DI 27 - TH, DOD 3).  This tornado was photographed and video taped.  The specific starting location was 42.62399,-87.86591, and the ending location was 42.63127,-87.81820.

The Sugar River at Brodhead reached minor flood stage, cresting at 5.65 feet the early afternoon of February 7th. Some roads were flooded in the Avon Township. In the Avon Bottoms area, flooding occurred in Sugar River Park.

The Fox River near New Munster reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11.66 feet the early afternoon of February 7th. Water surrounds a home near the intersection of Highway 50 and Highway W in the Town of Wheatland area. Water is in the back yards of some homes in the Village of Salem Lakes and Town of Wheatland areas. Floodwaters are about 6 inches deep over 77th Street in the Town of Wheatland area.
The Milwaukee County Medical Examiner's Office reported the death of a homeless man due to hypothermia. The 57-year-old man was found frozen in an abandoned vehicle and was missing for a month.

The Fox River at New Munster reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 13.38 feet the afternoon of March 15th. Floodwaters are into the lower levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland and Village of Salem Lakes along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Deep water is over a portion of 77th St. in the Town of Wheatland.

The Fox River at Burlington reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11.9 feet. Floodwaters are into Riverside Park in Burlington. Water is in the parking lot at Veteran's Terrace in Burlington. Water covers a portion of Brever Road about 4 miles south of Burlington. There is lowland flooding in the Burlington and Big Bend areas.

The Turtle Creek at Beloit reached minor flood stage, cresting at 9.07 feet the morning of March 14th.  Parts of Bootmaker Drive and Moccasin Trail are flooded. Colley Road is closed between Sager Lane and Brewster Ave. Floodwaters are in the backyards of some homes on East Ridge Road, Moccasin Drive, Boulder Ln, Rockfence Ln, Stonehedge Ln.

A significant ice jam at the Milwaukee River at Cedarburg resulted in ice impacting the  Pioneer Rd. bridge. The bridge was closed to traffic and was re-opened on March 18th. Other than lowland flooding, no other impacts were reported due to this ice jam.

An ice jam at the highway 33 bridge of the Milwaukee River at Saukville resulted in the closing of highway W between highway 33 and highway 57.  Highway W was flooded by several feet of water. Floodwaters were in the yards of homes along Mill St. Two water rescues occurred after both vehicles drove around the barriers and into the floodwaters on highway W.

A significant ice jam at the Milwaukee River at Waubeka closed the Cigrant Rd. bridge.  Just upstream from the bridge, 20 homes were impacted by flooding and 50 people were evacuated. The American Red Cross gave aid to the evacuees.  Much farther upstream, a lift station in the Village of Newburg was damaged. An Emergency Declaration was issued due to excessive flooding, although the flooding primarily was lowland.

The Sheboygan River flooded in the Town of Herman. Several homes and businesses were flooded on Main St. and Franklin Rd. The river was flowing over the Main St. bridge. An ice jam may have been occurring but was not confirmed.

Strong thunderstorms continued to affect the nearshore waters around Sheboygan through mid-afternoon.  The Sheboygan lakeshore weather station measured a wind gust to 41 knots in the mid-afternoon.

The Sheboygan River flooded low lying areas along the river due to several ice jams. The most impacted area was from just east of Kohler downstream to Kiwanis Park in Sheboygan. Portions of Indiana Ave. and New Jersey Ave., as well as other roads were closed due to flooding. At least one vehicle was submerged in the floodwaters on New Jersey Ave.

Ice jams on the various branches of the Fond du Lac river caused significant flooding in  the city of Fond du Lac. Most east/west roads across the river were closed due to flooding. A large section of highway 23 was flooded and closed in Fond du Lac. Hundreds of people were evacuated from homes and two apartment buildings. Water rescues were needed for those who were stranded in their homes or vehicles. The American Red Cross opened shelters to aid the flood victims. Schools were cancelled on Friday, March 15th.

The Fox River at Princeton reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 11.12 feet the late afternoon of March 24th. There is widespread flooding of lowland and wooded land in the Princeton area. Floodwaters affect Jefferson St. and the north end of Mechanic St. in Princeton. Floodwaters into yards of homes along S. Farmer St. and W Water St.

The Fox River at Berlin reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 15.45 feet during the early afternoon of March 27th. Some homes on Webster St. in Berlin are affected by the floodwaters. Riverside and Webster St. Parks are flooded.

Several county roads were closed due to the flooding of creeks, rivers, and lowlands. These roads were located near the villages of Dalton and Kingston, and near Utley and in the Township of Berlin. State highway 23 had a partial lane closure due to flooding between Princeton and Green Lake.

Thunderstorm wind gusts caused sporadic tree damage in parts of western Milwaukee. There was a report of a large tree with at least a 12 inch diameter base down 2 miles SSW of West Milwaukee. A large tree snapped at the base and there were several large branches down 2 miles ENE of Wauwatosa.
A peak wind gust of 51 knots (59 mph) was measured at General Mitchell International Airport in Milwaukee.

A line of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across southwest Washington County. There was a report of a snapped tree trunk around 4 inches in diameter near Hartford and a report of damage to house siding and a tree near Hubertus.

The WI River at Portage reached minor flood stage, cresting at 17.73 feet the early morning of March 28th. In the Blackhawk Park area in the Town of Caledonia, Old River Road is closed with water over it. West Lane Road in the Long Lake area is closed with about 4 feet of water over it in places. Wood Street is affected by floodwaters. In the Town of Dekorra, floodwaters are over portions of Oak Knoll Road and River Oaks Road. Several homes have water in the first floor and there is also flooding of outbuildings and yards.

Tornado was 1 of 19 tornadoes that occurred across central to east central Wisconsin on the afternoon of August 28th.  This was the strongest tornado of the event and went just north of the Village of Brownsville.  The worst damage was to a Canadian National Railway communications tower which was crumpled over.  Widespread straight line winds caused significant tree and crop damage across the county as well.  EF2 Damage occurred with the tornado further south at the onset of the tornado with EF1 damage occurring at the tail end of the tornado in southern Fond du Lac county.

Ice jams on Spring Creek and the Crawfish River led to significant flooding in the Lodi and Columbus areas, respectively.  Several businesses in the downtown area of Lodi were flooded, and roads were flooded and closed upstream and downstream of Spring Creek.   An ice jam at the highway 16/60 bridge in Columbus caused significant flooding near the river. 40 residents were evacuated from apartments and homes. Highway 16/60 was closed from County Road TT in Dodge County to highway 73 in Columbus.  Additional road closures occurred upstream on the branches of the Crawfish River near the Village of Fall River and Doylestown. Just southwest of Columbus, County Highway K was closed due to flooding from Robbins Creek. Farther north, the Fox River flooded, including Park Lake in Pardeeville, where severe erosion occurred to one property losing trees and soil along its shoreline.  Highway 44 was closed in a couple sections northeast of Pardeeville due to the flooding of the Fox River. In the southwest portion of the county, the Crystal Lake Campground and RV Park was evacuated due to the high levels of Crystal Lake on March 15th, but conditions improved by the next day.|Flooding also occurred in low lying areas across the county which closed a few additional rural roads, including south of Arlington and a small section of highway 188 in the Town of West Point near Lake Wisconsin.
Sheboygan lakeshore weather station measured a brief gust to 43 knots as scattered thunderstorms developed in the area.
A line of thunderstorms produced strong gusts at the Sheboygan lakeshore for several minutes.

events.event_narrative: Milwaukee General Mitchell Field airport (KMKE) reported a strong wind gust as a line of thunderstorms moved through.

The Crawfish River at Milford reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 9.39 feet the evening of March 20th. There is widespread flooding of agricultural land and lowland. There is widespread flooding in Riverbend Campground, about 5 miles upstream of Milford.

The Tri-County Airport was flooded on March 14th due to runoff from the nearby hills. The entire airport including its terminal building and main runway were flooded. The floodwaters did not recede until the last weekend in March. There was only minor flood damage to the runway and buildings.
Many streets on the west side of Sauk Prairie flooded and closed. Some homes surrounded by floodwaters and many basements flooded.

The South Branch of the Rock River reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 8.66 feet during the early morning of March 15th in Waupun. Water reached the support beam underneath the Fond du Lac St. bridge and it was closed. County Park Rd. was closed at the bridge as the Rock River flowed around the north end of the bridge, reconnecting with the river. Water was flowing around the north end of the city of Waupun Dam, reconnecting with the river. Gateway Dr. near the river was flooded and closed. Various parks along the river were flooded.

The Dodge County side of Columbus was evacuated near the Crawfish River due to flooding from an ice jam at the highway 16/60 bridge. The streets affected were Campbell St. and Baden St. Highway 28 just northeast of Theresa was closed from highway 175 to highway 41 due to flooding.  Several county roads were closed throughout the county.

Pumping of flooded roads was required on highway 83 in the Town of Merton, a portion of Barker Rd. in Brookfield, and a portion of highway K in the Oconomowoc area. A total of 2.5 million gallons of water was pumped off the roadways.
Highway 78 closed from Wiota to Gratiot due to flooding from the Pecatonica River and creeks.

The Pecatonica River at Darlington reached major flood stage, cresting at 17.62 feet the early evening of March 14th. Major urban flooding in the downtown area of Darlington affecting many businesses, although mitigation efforts resulted in less damage than past major floods. The main highways of 23 & 81 are closed as is Main St.  The Lafayette County fairgrounds is flooded. The Pecatonica River is flooding portions of Calamine upstream from Darlington.

The east branch of the Pecatonica River at Blanchardville reached major flood stage, cresting at 16.14 feet the early morning of March 15th. McKellar Park in Blanchardville is completely flooded including the swimming pool, tennis courts and football field. Nearby highway H is flooded and closed including the intersection of highway H and 78.
Highway 191 southeast of Dodgeville is closed from highway W to highway K due to the flooding of creeks. In addition, nearby highway 39 is also closed from highway F to highway K due to flooding.

The Baraboo River at Reedsburg reached minor flood stage, cresting at 15.45 feet the early afternoon of March 15th. Floodwaters affect Granite Ave. and South Webb Ave. along the river. There is general inundation of lowland in the Reedsburg area. The walking path in Webb Park and Smith Conservancy is covered with water. The Public Works yard is under 18-24 inches of water.

The Baraboo River at Rock Springs reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 22.17 feet the early morning of March 15th. Floodwaters affect the edges of Highways DD, 154 and 136 in Rock Springs as well as Busser Park along Highway 136. Water is about 3 feet deep in the baseball diamond in Fireman's Park along Highway DD. Floodwaters affect some businesses, including the Post Office on Highway 154.

The Baraboo River at Baraboo reached minor flood stage, cresting at 20.68 feet the evening of March 17th. Floodwaters affect a trailer rental business and a road wayside park about 5 miles downstream from the gauge near the Highway 33 bridge. Floodwaters also affect an auto auction business near I90/94.

The Black Earth Creek at Mazomanie reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11.66 feet the late evening of March 14th. Floodwaters affect Curtiss St. and other streets on the northeast side of Mazomanie, including County Road Y.

The Rock River at Jefferson reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 11.5 feet the late morning of March 16th. Floodwaters affect low lying areas of residential and business property in Jefferson. Water approaches the intersection of Main St. and E. Dane St. South Center Ave. near the river is flooded and E. Riverview Drive near the wastewater plant is flooded and closed. Flooding in Riverfront Park.

The Rock River at Fort Atkinson reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 17.24 feet the late morning of March 24th. This flooding continued into early April. Numerous roads closed: Sinnissippi Dr., Bark River Rd. from Kutz Rd. to Rock River Rd., Rock River Rd. from Milwaukee Ave. to Hwy 106.  Ralph Rd. impacted. Floodwaters surround a few homes and businesses close to the river at the end of Vets Lane near the intersection of Highway 106 and Blackhawk Island Rd. North Shore Rd. is closed. The river walkway in Fort Atkinson is flooded and closed.

The Rock River at Lake Koshkonong reached major flood stage, cresting at 11.51 feet the early morning of March 25th. This flooding continued into April. Lake Koshkonong merges with Mud Lake and the Rock River on the east side of the lake. There is knee-deep water over Blackhawk Island Rd. and Lamp Rd. is flooded.  Flooding on Oxbow Bend Rd. in the Town of Koshkonong.

The Rock River at Newville reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 7.6 feet the morning of March 26th. Floodwaters surround some homes near East Mallwood Dr. and are into yards and roads across eastern Newville.

The Rock River at Afton reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11.07 feet the early afternoon of March 25th. This flooding continued into April. Floodwaters affect a home on South Christian Rd. on the east side of the river in the Afton area. Floodwaters affect a road in Riverside Park on the north side of Janesville and South River Rd. from the south side of Janesville toward Afton. There is widespread lowland and agricultural  flooding in the Afton and Janesville areas.

Many roads were flooded and closed in the Township of Avon due to the flooding of the Sugar River and due to lowland flooding. Portions of other roads were closed into central and northeast Rock Co., more specifically in the townships of Spring Valley, Rock, Plymouth, Fulton, and Johnstown due to lowland flooding and creek flooding. A portion of highway 51 was flooded and closed in Edgerton.

Portions of many roads flooded and closed mainly over the western half of Dane Co. More specifically, flooded roads in the deeper valleys and near creeks and the Sugar River. Large portions of highway 78 was flooded and closed and highway 69 from US 151 to near Paoli. Highway 19 was closed at the intersection with highway KP. Portions of South Point Rd. on the far west side of Madison was flooded and closed. Several streets and adjacent yards in De Forest were flooded by the Yahara River. Voluntary evacuations occurred in De Forest.
The Sheboygan lakeshore weather station measured a wind gust to 40 knots as strong thunderstorms moved through.

The Pecatonica River at Martintown reached major flood stage, cresting at 22.41 feet during the early afternoon of March 16th. Some homes in the Martintown area have floodwaters in their basements and first floors with major damage. Martintown Road and West River Road in Martintown are flooded. The Pecatonica River was flooding upstream to the border with Lafayette County. In Browntown, Hwy 11 is limited to one lane between highway M and Cadiz Spring Rd. Portions of Highway MM and West Indies Road are flooded.

The entire Sugar River was flooding from just south of Belleville, downstream to the Avon Township of Rock Co. The Sugar River at Albany reached moderate flood stage, and at Brodhead reached major flood stage. Various roads were closed near the river in the Attica, Albany, and Brodhead areas. These included portions of highway X, Schneeberger Rd., Tin Can Rd., and highway T near the Avon Township of Rock Co. A water rescue occurred on Schneeberger Rd.  In Albany, portions of South Water St. floods from a backup storm sewer. Floodwaters affect the basements of some homes along South Water St. and in the basements of a few businesses on North Water St.  Floodwaters affect the back yards of some homes along South Mill St. and South Water St. Floodwaters are into Village Park. Farther to the west in the Townships of Jordan and Monroe, lowland and creek flooding resulted in the closure of highway Y from highway 81 to M. Klondike Rd. is flooded and closed in the Town of Jordan.

Due to the near record high water levels on Lake Michigan, the Milwaukee River has also risen resulting in basement flooding in nearby restaurants and businesses. The Milwaukee Health Department ordered the temporary closure of two restaurants. The basement flooding or the use pumps for mitigation will continue through the summer and beyond until the lake and river levels drop.

A lake cruiser on Lake Monona had its canopy blown-off from straight-line winds. The boat did make it to shore and the 33 occupants were not injured. In Monona, large tree branches and power lines were downed, including one large Oak tree.
A sailboat and kayak were overturned by straight-line winds near the south shore of Green Lake. Both occupants were uninjured.

The Fox River at Berlin remained in flood much of the month after cresting at moderate flood stage toward the end of March. Some homes on Webster St. in Berlin are affected by floodwaters. Riverside and Webster St. parks are flooded.

The Rock River at Fort Atkinson crested at moderate flood stage in late March and  continued to flood into the 1st week of April. The river walkway in Fort Atkinson is flooded and closed.  On the west side of Fort Atkinson, the southern portion of Rock River Park is flooded and Sinissippi Dr. is closed.  On the east side of Fort Atkinson, Bark River Rd. from Kutz Road to Rock River Rd. is flooded and closed. Rock River Rd. from highway 106 to the Fort Atkinson city limits is flooded and closed.

The Rock River at Lake Koshkonong crested at major flood stage in late March and  continued to flood into April 9th. There is widespread flooding of roads and docks in the Town of Koshkonong and the Town of Sumner including Vets Lane, Blackhawk Island Rd., and Oxbow Bend Rd.

The Rock River at Afton crested in late March at minor flood stage. The minor flooding continued until April 12th. Floodwaters affect the property of a home on South Christian Rd. on the east side of the river in the Afton area. Floodwaters affect Riverside Park on the north side of Janesville, and South River Rd. on the south side of Janesville. There is widespread lowland and agricultural flooding in the Afton and Janesville areas.

The Wisconsin River at Portage crested at minor flood stage in late March and continued into early April. In the Blackhawk Park area in the Town of Caledonia, Wood St. is affected by floodwaters. Old River Rd. and Blackhawk Rd. is flooded and closed. Near Long Lake, West Lane Rd. and West Lake Rd. are flooded and closed. County Highway V and Oak Knoll Road in the Town of Dekorra have water up to the edge of the pavement. A few homes in the Town of Dekorra have water in the first floor, and there is also flooding of outbuildings and yards.

The WI River at Portage reached major flood stage, cresting at 20.08 feet the late evening of April 21st.  Much of the Blackhawk Park and Long Lake areas and its numerous roads and some homes are flooded. Some evacuations occurred in these areas. In the city of Portage, portions of  W. Conant St. and Summit St. are flooded including the boat launch. Water rises through the ground and floods portions of Sunset and Franklin Streets. The Fire Department built a berm on Summit  St. which prevented the expansion of flooding into more residential areas. Basement flooding was occurring |for homes near the floodwaters. Upstream from Portage, Levee Rd. is closed from highway 33 just south of Portage to Schepp Rd. in Sauk Co. Residents living on Levee Rd. were evacuated due to some erosion of the Caledonia levee which protects the area from substantial flooding. Portions of River Shores Rd. was also flooded on the east side of the river. Downstream from Portage in the Town of Dekorra, around a dozen homes are flooded on highway V. Portions of highway V, River Oaks Rd., and Oak Knoll Dr. are flooded. Across the river and slightly upstream from the Town of Dekorra, a portion of Thunderbird Rd. is flooded.

Flash flooding of creeks and some roads from La Valle to Reedsburg after several inches of rain. A road washout occurred at the intersection of highway 33 and Twin Pine Rd. Babb Creek flooded the backyards of residential homes in Reedsburg. Some basement flooding occurred in Reedsburg.
Highway 12 in Sauk City is closed due to heavy rainfall and flash flooding after a quick couple inches of rain.

Pershing Park Drive in the City of Racine was closed due to rocks and debris being thrown onto the roadways by high waves.  The gravel parking area adjacent to the park will need to be re-graded due to the debris. Time included is when the duration of the strongest onshore winds at the Racine airport (KRAC).
Flash flooding of some streets in urban and rural areas especially in Twin Lakes, Paddock Lake, and the town of Bristol. Some roads were closed due to the high water.
