Approximately 100 people were displaced when an apartment building was struck by lightning causing a fire. The 42 unit apartment building was a total loss. One resident was rescued from the third floor and one fireman was injured. Two residents were also injured.
Multiple road closures due to flash flooding in Plain, Prairie du Sac, Sauk City, and other locations over southern Sauk County after a quick few inches of rain.

Flash flooding of some streets in Dodgeville and Mineral Point and numerous roads flooded throughout the county. Mud and rocks on a portion of highway 130/133 in the far northern portion of the county.
Flash flooding of roads in Darlington and other townships throughout the county. Numerous road closures were needed due to the high water.
Flash flooding and closures of numerous streets in Janesville. This includes the intersection of Lexington Dr. and Mount Zion Ave. and County Highway D south of Janesville.
Flash flooding and closures of multiple roads across the southern portion of the county. Flash flooding of the White River led to flooded yards and a trailer being swept away.
Flash flooding and closures of multiple roads from New Berlin to Muskego.

The Root River Parkway and nearby roads and intersections were closed due to the flash flooding of the Root River. A vehicle became disabled in the floodwaters. In addition to street flooding, yards, basements, and garages flooded especially in Franklin. Multiple reports of standing water on the freeway system and side streets throughout much of the county.
Flash flooding of some streets in Kenosha including water in the basement of the public safety building.

Various roads remained flooded and closed across the county. This included a portion of County Road H in the eastern part of the county and 236th Ave. in Paddock Lake. Rising waters on Lily Lake resulted in waterfront properties surrounded by high water.

Rising waters on Delavan Lake resulted in pier planks and boats breaking free. Rising waters on Geneva Lake caused water to flow over the dam, thereby flooding the White River and a nearby park and nature preserve in Lake Geneva. Some streets were closed near the White River. Other roads over southern Walworth County remained flooded and closed.

The Fox River at New Munster reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 13.15 feet the evening of September 14th. Water is up to the first floor levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland and Village of Salem Lakes along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. There is flooding on 77th St. Floodwaters surround a home near the intersection of highway 50 and W.

The Root River at Franklin reached minor flood stage, cresting at 9.08 feet the evening of September 13th.  A portion of Oakwood Road in southern Milwaukee County is flooded and closed. There is flooding to agricultural land.

The Turtle Creek at Beloit reached minor flood stage, cresting at 9.72 feet the morning of September 14th. Floodwaters surround a power substation on Colley Road. Colley Road is closed between Sager Lane and Brewster Ave. Floodwaters are also in the backyards of some homes on Arrowhead Drive, East Ridge Road, Mocassin Drive, Boulder Lane, Rockfence Lane and Stonehedge Lane. Parts of Bootmaker Drive and Moccasin Trail are flooded.

The Pecatonica River at Darlington reached minor flood stage, cresting at 14.31 feet during the early afternoon of September 14th. Floodwaters cover a portion of Main Street in Darlington. A part of the Lafayette County Fairgrounds is flooded as well as agricultural land in the area.

The Pecatonica River at Martintown reached minor flood stage, cresting at 15.38 feet the  morning of September 18th. Floodwaters affect Martintown Road and West River Road in the Martintown area. Upstream in Browntown, floodwaters affect highway MM and West Indies Road. The river continued to flood into October.

Sporadic damage noted along the path of the weak tornado along the southwest side of Fort Atkinson.  Clearly started in a corn field that had corn stalks pulled up and deposited on a farm house across the street.  Ended on the southern side of the city where a few houses sustained damage, mainly from trees falling on them.

Damage from this tornado came within a mile and a half of NWS Milwaukee to the north.  Mainly tree damage from this tornado, though one house did have siding and window damage from the debris blown into it.

Damage was mainly to trees though a few outbuildings were damaged down the road from NWS Milwaukee.  One garage had antique sports cars stored in it which had its door blown in and the wall push out, but was just sitting on cinder blocks.  Extensive tree damage near School Section Lake and another shed toward the end of the path.

Southbound lanes of I-43 flooded and closed from highway D at Belgium to highway H near Port Washington. Several roads flooded and impassable in the northern portion of Ozaukee County.

Extensive street flooding on Washington Ave. with people sitting on top of their cars to avoid the floodwaters. Other street flooding across the Madison area.

The Fox River at New Munster reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 13.63 feet the afternoon of October 4th. Floodwaters are into the lower levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland and Village of Salem Lakes along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Relatively deep floodwaters are over 77th St. in the Town of Wheatland.

The Milwaukee River at Cedarburg reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 13 feet during the late morning on October 3rd. Floodwaters affect Island Drive and Shoreland Parkway in the Mequon area. Water is over Elm St., Green Bay Rd., North Cedarburg Rd., and portions of the village park in Thiensville.

The Milwaukee River at Saukville reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 15.22 feet during the morning on October 2nd. Floodwaters affect parts of Green Bay Ave., Park St., Mill St., S. Riverside Drive and N. Riverside Drive in and near Saukville. Parks that are flooded are Peninsula Park, Grady Park and Schowalter Park.

The Milwaukee River at Waubeka reached minor flood stage, cresting at 9.61 feet during the late afternoon of October 2nd. Water approaches some homes in Waubeka in the area of Second Street and County Highway Z. There is significant flooding downstream in Waubedonia Park and Marie Kraus Park.

The Sheboygan River at Sheboygan reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 10.53 feet during the early afternoon on October 2nd. About 3 miles west of Sheboygan Airport, Woodland Road is closed between Rio Road and Willow Road. A section of Alpine Road near the Sheboygan Airport is closed. There is flooding in River Park in Sheboygan Falls and in Esslingen Park in Sheboygan.

The Turtle Creek at Beloit reached minor flood stage, cresting at 8.39 feet at noon on October 3rd. Colley Road is closed between Sager Lane and Brewster Avenue. Floodwaters are in the backyards of some homes on East Ridge Road, Moccasin Drive, Boulder Lane, Rockfence Lane, Stonehedge Lane.

The Crawfish River at Milford reached minor flood stage, cresting at 8.38 feet during the early morning of October 9th. There is widespread flooding of agricultural land and lowland. There is widespread flooding in Riverbend Campground, about 5 miles upstream of Milford.

The east branch of the Pecatonica River at Blanchardville reached minor flood stage, cresting at 13.75 feet the early afternoon of October 3rd.  McKellar Park in Blanchardville is completely flooded including the swimming pool and tennis courts. Oak St., highway H and Water St. are closed near the park.

The Pecatonica River at Darlington reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 15.88 feet the late morning of October 3rd.  Highways 23 and 81 in Darlington are flooded and closed as is Main Street. The Lafayette County fairgrounds are flooded. Several miles upstream, there is flooding in Calamine and farther north Ferndale Rd. is flooded and closed.

The Pecatonica River at Martintown reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 18.83 feet the early morning of October 7th. This is a continuation of flooding that began on September 15th. Some homes in the Martintown area have floodwaters in their basements and first floors. Martintown Road and West River Road are flooded. Upstream in Browntown, Highway MM and West Indies Road are flooded.

Spring Creek at Lodi reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 7.3 feet the morning of October 2nd. Floodwaters affect Goeres Park including the pool, and Habermann Park including the baseball diamond. Floodwaters approach the Public Works garage.

The Black Earth Creek at Mazomanie reached minor flood stage, cresting at 10.95 feet the afternoon of October 2nd. Floodwaters affect Curtiss Street and other streets on the northeast side of Mazomanie. There is also general lowland flooding in the Mazomanie area.

The Baraboo River at Baraboo reached minor flood stage, cresting at 18.23 feet the morning of October 4th. Tritz Rd. was flooded and closed near the intersection with highway 33.  Floodwaters affected a portion of the parking lot of a trailer rental business just east of the highway 33 bridge over the Baraboo River. A nearby wayside park was also partially flooded.

The Sugar River at Brodhead reached minor flood stage, cresting at 7.53 feet the evening of October 4th. Some roads are flooded about 6 miles downstream in Avon Township of Rock County. In the Avon Bottoms area of Rock County, flooding is occurring in Sugar River Park.

The south branch of the Rock River at Waupun reached minor flood stage, cresting at 7.83 feet by late morning on October 2nd. Water reaches the support beams underneath the Fond du Lac St. bridge and it is closed. Gateway Dr. is flooded and closed. Water starts to over top the dam at Shaler Park. County Park Rd. is closed at the bridge as the river flows around the north end of bridge. Various parks and associated roads are closed along the river.

A glaze of ice on roadways from freezing drizzle. Numerous vehicle slide-offs and accidents especially on I-94. Westbound I-94 was closed from Johnson Creek to Oconomowoc due to the icy conditions and accidents.

A glaze of ice on roadways from freezing drizzle. The sheriff's department responded to 38 accidents and 8 vehicle slide-offs across the county. The worst area was westbound I-94 west of Oconomowc which was closed, and highway 16.
A glaze of ice on roadways from freezing drizzle. Some vehicle slide-offs and accidents occurred.
A glaze of ice on roadways from freezing drizzle. Some vehicle slide-offs and accidents occurred especially on I-41 south of Fond du Lac.

The Rock River at Jefferson reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 11 feet the morning of October 12th. Floodwaters affect low lying areas of residential and business property in Jefferson. Water approaches the intersection of Main St. and E. Dane St.  The retention pond at this intersection is full. South Center Ave. near the river is flooded and Riverview Drive near the wastewater plant is flooded. Riverfront Park is flooded.

The Rock River at Fort Atkinson reached minor flood stage, cresting at 16.83 feet the afternoon of October 12th. The following roads in the Fort Atkinson area are flooded and closed: Sinissippi drive, Vets Lane, Bark River Road from Kutz Road to Rock River Road.  Rock River Road from Highway 106 to the Fort Atkinson city limits. The river walkway in Fort Atkinson becomes flooded and is closed.

The Rock River at Afton reached minor flood stage, cresting at 10.47 feet the evening of October 15th. The flooding continued into November.  Floodwaters affect Riverside Park on the north side of Janesville and South River Road on the south side of Janesville. Floodwaters affect a home on South Christian Road on the east side of the river in the Afton area. There is extensive lowland and agricultural land flooding in the Afton and Janesville areas.

The Rock River at Lake Koshkonong reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11 feet the late afternoon of October 15th. There is widespread flooding of roads and docks in the Town of Koshkonong and the Town of Sumner, including Blackhawk Island Road and Oxbow Bend Road.

The Rock River at Newville reached minor flood stage, cresting at 7.15 feet the late evening of October 14th. Floodwaters surround some homes near East Mallwood Drive and are into yards and roads across eastern Newville.
A marine contact sent WFO MKX images of flooding in a parking lot and boat ramp launch area adjoining the north channel in downtown Kenosha, which leads into Lake Michigan.

Flood waters due to high waves estimated 6 to 8 feet and near record Lake Michigan water levels spread across the Port of Milwaukee, causing the Port to close late in the morning on January 11th.  Carferry Drive and Lincoln Memorial Drive were closed leading into the Port of Milwaukee.  About 60 to 70 percent of Jones Island where Port of Milwaukee is located was flooded.  The flood water stripped dock wall material and covered railroad tracks with a foot of ice on Jones Island.  The Port of Milwaukee reopened 48 hours later on Monday, January 13th.  Flood erosion damage took place at other locations along the Milwaukee County shore: ||- South Shore Yacht Club: Damage to piers and docks.  Damage to break wall located just outside the club. |- Partial washout of Oak Leaf walking trail along South Shore Drive.  Also damage to trail near art museum.|- Riverfront boat launch damage.|- Veterans Park: Concrete washout of lakeshore.|- McKinley Marina gas dock collapse. Also integrity of parking lot and boat launch compromised.|- Warnimont Golf Course - 20' x 30' section of bluff collapse. ||Also section of North Point Light parking lot collapse and washout into lake. Also, 50' x 50' section of bluff collapse at Bay View and Lake Parks.
Sheboygan police closed Broughton Drive between Michigan Avenue and Barrett Street due to unsafe road conditions caused by lakeshore flooding.
Lakeshore erosion at Carre Hogel Park (200' shoreline), Pershing Drive (900' shoreline), North of Zoo Beach (260' embankment/bluff and shoreline erosion), and Shoop Park (50' erosion).
Port Washington Director of Public Works reported lakeshore flood damage to walkway and ramp leading to breakwall.

Near record high Lake Michigan water levels along with strong winds and resultant high waves peaking at 10 to 15 feet caused considerable erosion and lakeshore flood damage along the Kenosha County lakeshore.  ||Some of the damage in the county included: ||Kemper Center County Park in Kenosha was severely damaged along the Lake Michigan shoreline due to high winds and waves.   One thousand, five hundred feet of shoreline was damaged.  Severe destruction occurred where voids in the shoreline were created, causing displaced rock and earth material.  ||The Kenosha shoreline between 71st Street and 76th Street was damaged.  A sinkhole developed and caused the shoreline to collapse in two locations.  Damage also occurred on the Kenosha Harbor walls and promenade due to high waves of at least 10 feet.  Lakeshore flooding also closed Kenosha streets including First Avenue, 50th Street, Fourth Avenue and 45th street.||The Village of Pleasant Prairie sustained lakeshore damage on Lake Shore Drive between 107th St and 113th Street, to about 1300 feet of shoreline.  A stream outlet just north of 110th St. was buried by lakeshore flooding and erosion, which resulted in flooding on upstream properties A 15-inch corrugated metal culvert end section required emergency excavation to alleviate the flooding.  Damage was also done at the South Beach area, Chiwaukee Beach and Prairie Shores Beach.  ||Lakeshore erosion also caused a Pleasant Prairie home to teeter on the edge of bluff overlooking Lake Michigan.

A 65 year-old man was found dead in the morning on his snow covered driveway in Glendale. The Milwaukee County Medical Examiner determined the cause of death as hypothermia. He was last seen the prior afternoon. Temperatures were mainly in the 20 degree Fahrenheit range during this time, and the man was not dressed appropriately for the cold.
A 73 year-old woman was found dead in her unheated home. The Milwaukee County Medical Examiner determined the probable cause of death as hypothermia.

A 72 year-old man was found conscious and crawling on his driveway in the morning. He was taken to the hospital where he died. The Milwaukee County Medical Examiner determined the probable cause of death as hypothermia. He had a core body temperature of 79 degrees Fahrenheit.

The WI River at Portage reached moderate flood stage due to melting snow and rainfall. It crested the early morning of April 1st at 18.18 feet. Numerous roads are flooded in the Blackhawk Park and Long Lake areas across the river from Portage. Floodwaters surround seasonal homes along Old River Rd. Water is at the base of the  Caledonia/Lewiston Levee near Old River Rd. In the Town of Dekorra, water is over portions of River Oaks Rd. and Oak Knoll Dr., while about a dozen homes are flooded on Hwy V.  This flooding continued into early April.

The WI River at Portage reached moderate flood stage due to melting snow and rainfall. It crested the early morning of April 1st at 18.18 feet. Numerous roads are flooded in the Blackhawk Park and Long Lake areas across the river from Portage. Floodwaters surround seasonal homes along Old River Rd. Water is at the base of the Caledonia/Lewiston Levee near Old River Rd. In the Town of Dekorra, water is over portions of River Oaks Rd. and Oak Knoll Dr., while about a dozen homes are flooded on Hwy V.
A lightning strike to a radio antenna on a home on National Avenue damaged a breadmaker, interior wiring, and electrical outlets.  However , there was no fire.

A lightning bolt struck a tree and air conditioning unit of a home in New Berlin.  The current was carried into the basement of the home and the resultant fire was contained mostly in the basement.  Electrical wiring was damaged. Smoke damage was noted elsewhere in the home.

The Fox River at New Munster rose above flood stage early on March 3rd and finally went below flood stage on March 9th.  It crested at 12.01 feet at 1750 CST on March 4th, or 2.01 feet over flood stage.  The typical bottom-land flooding occurred.  A couple homes sustained water damage to their basement contents.  Many other rivers and streams in south-central and southeast Wisconsin rose to near bankfull or almost flood stage during the period of March 3rd-9th.  Additionally, many of the same rivers would rise above flood stage during the March 21st-23rd period and remain above flood stage into April, 2008.
Sixty-Seventh Dr. was closed between 58th Rd. and Mill Ave. due to high water on a portion of the road.
High water around 1.5-2.0 feet deep at the intersection of 38th St. and highway D.

The Fox River at New Munster reached minor flood stage, cresting at 12.46 feet on May 1st. This flooding continued into the early evening of May 5th. Water is up to the first floor levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland and the Village of Salem Lakes along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Floodwaters surround a home at the intersection of Highway 50 and Highway W in the Town of Wheatland area. Water is about 12 inches deep over 77th Street in the Town of Wheatland area.

The Root River Canal at Raymond reached minor flood stage, cresting at 10.57 feet on April 30th. This flooding continued into May 1st. Floodwaters cover a baseball diamond on 6 Mile Road. There is extensive flooding to lowland and agricultural land in the Town of Raymond.
Several large trees were blown down in New Berlin due to gusty winds and saturated soils. Another large tree was blown down in Brookfield.
One large tree blown down in Caledonia.

A wooden swing set was blown over.

Water is up to the first floor levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland and the Village of Salem Lakes along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Floodwaters surround a home at the intersection of Highway 50 and Highway W in the Town of Wheatland area. Water is about 12 inches deep over 77th Street in the Town of Wheatland area.

The Root River Canal at Raymond reached minor flood stage, cresting at 10.57 feet on April 30th. This flooding continued into May 1st. Floodwaters cover a baseball diamond on 6 Mile Road. There is extensive flooding to lowland and agricultural land in the Town of Raymond.
Four horse shelters collapsed by downburst winds.
High tension power lines down along a 1 mile stretch of County Road V.
A swath of tree and power line damage, some falling in roads.  A couple sheds blown off foundations.

Portions of Swift Lake, Lake Lorraine, Lake Wandawega, and the village of Walworth flooded after 2-3 inches of rain and resultant runoff into already high lake levels from last autumn. This flooded a small number of homes and other structures.
Water over roads in low-lying areas all over the county with some closures. Many people in the City of Sheboygan had water in their basements due to the storm sewer backing up.

Numerous flooding reports all over the county with some road closures. Numerous basements flooded in Port Washington. A retaining wall collapsed onto an elderly woman in Port Washington, killing her. Two drivers rescued driving into deep water underneath a railroad bridge on Spring St. and Sunset Rd. in Port Washington.

West Allis PD rescued a stranded driver via a boat on the Root River Parkway, whose car stalled in relatively deep water from the flooding of the nearby Root River. Another car stalled in relatively deep water at 112th and Cleveland Ave. from the flooding of the Root River. The Root River and other creeks and rivers throughout Milwaukee remained high or flooded through the night. Some of the adjacent roads, yards, and basements also flooded.
In New Berlin there were numerous flooded streets, basements, and elevator shafts. |A portion of 130th St. was closed due to road buckling.
A quick 1-1.5 inches of rain led some street flooding in Beloit. Notably at the intersection of South Afton Rd. and Newark Rd., and on McKinley Ave.

The Root River at Racine reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 7.9 feet during the early afternoon of May 19th. Lincoln Park and Horlick Park in Racine are flooded and closed. Floodwaters are in the backyards of some homes and there is some basement flooding.

The Root River at Raymond and across northeast Racine County flooded after several inches of rainfall in the basin. The Root River at Raymond crested at 10.97 feet on May 18th. Floodwaters are in the backyards of some homes in the Town of Raymond. There is widespread flooding of lowland and agricultural land throughout the basin.  Floodwaters cover a baseball diamond on 6 Mile Road. On May 18th, Nicholson Road, which crosses the Root River near the Racine and Milwaukee County line, was closed due to flooding. Husher Creek, which flows into the Root River, also flooded and was covering Highway 38 south of Seven Mile Road.

The Root River at Franklin reach minor flood stage, cresting at 9.52 feet the morning of May 18th. On May 18th, the Root River Parkway at Layton Avenue in Greenfield had to close due to flooding. A driver drove his vehicle into floodwaters which caused his vehicle to stall. The driver did exit the scene safely.  The Root River also flooded and closed both the north and southbound lanes of Wisconsin 241 over far southeast Franklin the morning of May 18th. The road remained closed into the afternoon.  A portion of Oakwood Road is flooded and closed. There is widespread flooding to agricultural land along the basin.
Sheboygan lakeshore observation reported strong wind gusts as thunderstorms moves across the near shore waters.

The Sheboygan River reached moderate flood stage, cresting at 11.07 feet the morning of May 18th. About 3 miles west of Sheboygan Airport, Woodland Road is flooded and closed between Rio Road and Willow Road due to the flooding of the Sheboygan River. Sections of Alpine Road and Meadowlark Road in the Sheboygan Falls area are flooded and closed. Floodwaters affect Kiwanis and Esslingen Parks in Sheboygan. Other roads and low lying areas are flooded in closed due to areal flooding from the several inches of rain that had fallen.

The Fox River at New Munster reached minor flood stage, cresting at 12.97 feet the early morning of May 19th. Water is up to the first floor levels of some homes in the Town of Wheatland, and the Village of Salem Lakes along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Floodwaters surround a home at the intersection of Highway 50 and Highway W in the Town of Wheatland area. Water is about 12 inches deep over 77th Street in the Town of Wheatland area.

The Milwaukee River near Cedarburg reached minor flood stage, cresting at 11.8 feet during the early afternoon on May 19th. Water approaches some homes along Klug Lane just south of Highway C in Thiensville. Water is near some homes along Island Drive and Shoreland Parkway in the Mequon area.

Heavy rainfall and persistent northeast winds causing high waves resulted in significant lakeshore bluff erosion in parts of Ozaukee County, along Lake Michigan.  In the Town of Grafton, an estimated 4 feet of bluff eroded causing the foundation of one home on Lake Shore Road and Pioneer Road to be exposed.  A significant mud slide occurred at Lion's Den Gorge State Park that did necessitate the rescue of two hikers that were trying to retrieve a dog.  The hikers had only minor injuries.  There was also a hill slide at the Port Washington High School/Community Pool.  This resulted in a compromised roadway.  Small sections of the bluff have failed up and down the Ozaukee county shoreline, including Upper Lake Park in Port Washington.

A young swimmer and the man who tried to save him died due to drowning at McKinley Beach at the Milwaukee lakeshore.  Breezy south winds resulted in moderate waves and dangerous underwater currents along the shore, and near piers and breakwalls.  Wave heights were estimated to be 2 to 4 feet at the time of the incident.
Man drowns in water off McKinley Beach after rescuing two family members from deep water, waves and currents.

Three to seven inches of rain from persistent thunderstorms resulted in the flash flooding of creeks, streets, parks, and residential yards in southern Milwaukee County. This included the communities of West Allis, Greenfield, Oak Creek, Franklin, and others in southern Milwaukee County.  Many streets were impassable and closed. Many vehicles were stranded in 2 to 4 feet of floodwaters. Portions of I-43 were closed due to flooding.  Many yards and basements were flooded especially when the floodwaters rose from the streets into the yards.  Oak Creek at South Milwaukee rapidly rose and nearly reached moderate flood stage.

Many roads impassible in Portage from flash flooding. Many vehicles stranded or flowing within the deep floodwaters with several water rescues executed.  Also, yards and basements flooded in Portage. Elsewhere in northern Columbia County, road and culvert washouts on highway P east of Pardeeville, and in the townships of Fort Winnebago and Lewiston. Rising waters on Swan Lake flooded out some homes on the northwest side of the lake. Portions of the Fox River flooded from northeast Columbia County to Pardeeville. The Fox River floodwaters flooded a portion of highway 44 northeast of Marcellon. The Pardeeville DPW sandbagged the sanitary sewer manholes to reduce the constant running of the lift stations.

Weak tornado started on the southeast end of Geneva Lake and went through the southeast side of Lake Geneva.  Mainly tree damage along the path, but some minor structural damage in the business district bounded by highways 120, 50 and 12.  Path appeared to end just south of the Grand Geneva resort.

Tornado started in NW Lake County Illinois where some house and structural damage occurred just south of the WI/IL border.  The tornado then crossed into Wisconsin and knocked hundreds of trees down (trunks snapped and uprooted) at Promised Land camp.  Tornado continued northeast toward the southwest side of Camp Lake where shingle damage was noted on a few houses.  Tornado then crossed Camp Lake and exited it on the northeast side where more tree damage was noted.  Some pontoon boats and docks were toppled on Camp Lake.  Tornado was embedded within a line of storms that also had winds of 50-60 mph.
Four to six inches of rain led to some minor road flooding between La Valle and Reedsburg. A section of Birchwood Rd. was washed out and closed on the west side of Lake Delton.

Spring Creek at Lodi reached major flood stage, cresting around 7.6 feet the morning of October 23rd. Floodwaters affect Goeres Park including the pool, and water approaches the Public Works garage, and Habermann park including the baseball diamond.

The flash flooding of various creeks and lowlands caused flooding on some some rural roads across southern Sauk County. This included but not limited to, water over County Highway C near highway 12, water over highway 60 in the Town of Prairie du Sac, water over County Highway G near the Spring Green Nature Preserve.  There was also street flooding near the Sauk Prairie High School.

Strong winds and high waves on Lake Winnebago resulted in a canoe capsizing during the evening of March 29th.  The canoe was located about one mile north of the city of Fond du Lac and the Fond du Lac river outlet, on Lake Winnebago.  Two young male canoeists, neither wearing a personal flotation device, fell into the cold lake water and drowned.  The Lake Winnebago water temperature was estimated to be 42 degrees F. Winds were gusting as high as 40 knots near the time of the event, and waves on the southern end of Lake Winnebago were estimated to be 4 to 5 feet.  The victims were located several days later on March 31st and April 1st.  Strong and gusty south winds had been occurring over the lake and vicinity since late morning.

A long-tracked, partially rain-wrapped, tornado traveled through mostly rural areas of Columbia County and affected only a small portion of one village; otherwise property damage would have been more extensive.  This tornado spun up about 2.75 miles east of Dekorra, just northwest of the intersection of STH 51 and CTH VJ, near Columbia Lake.  It then tracked east-northeast through the far southeast reaches of the village of Wyocena, and crossed STH 22 just north of Patchin Road.  It then moved through the intersection of CTH G and W. Hill Road, where the last structural damage to a couple barns and home occurred.  Thereafter, this tornado tracked more northeast through rural areas (crossing STH 33 midway between Cunningham Road and Englehart Road), and eventually exited Columbia County just east of North County Line Road and Sterk Road.  It continued for a few more miles through southeastern Green Lake County.  Based on ground damage evidence, this tornado briefly lifted a couple times when it was north of STH 33.  Most of the structural damage occurred south and southeast of Wyocena. Otherwise the rural damage consisted of uprooted trees or broken branches.  At least two trained spotters video taped the tornado.||The Columbia County Emergency Management situation report indicated that 4 residential homes sustained minor damage, and 1 home suffered major damage.  Additionally, 2 farm buildings had minor damage, 2 suffered major damage, and 3 were destroyed.  The report estimated that private sector damage totaled about $550,000 (excluding electrical line damage).  Public sector debris clearance totaled $3500, and protective measures totaled $1000.  The Sheriff's Office had to close down 4 roads until power lines and trees could be cleared.  Electrical line replacement is estimated at about $50,000.  The lat-long pairs of numbers for this tornado segment in Columbia County include: N43.46179/W89.41637, N43.49223/W89.27809, N43.54813/W89.18491, and N43.63221/W89.06693.  On the EF-scale, DI #1 (SBO) was used with a DOD of 6, for an EF-rating of EF1 and an wind estimate of about 100 mph (87 knots).

A narrow band of heavy snow showers produced whiteout conditions and slick roads over portions of I-41 in Washington County for a period of 45 minutes to 90 minutes. Numerous multi-vehicle accidents were reported on I-41 near highway 144 and Cedar Creek Road, which included a crash involving 30 vehicles and another with 48 vehicles. 1 death was reported. 12 people were injured and sent to the hospital. Another 26 people were treated at the scene.
A cluster of trees fell on a garage in Delavan, causing significant damage.  Afternoon wind gusts measured around 45 mph over the region.

This tornado segment is a continuation of a long-tracked tornado that spun up east of Dekorra in Columbia County and affected the Wyocena area.  It entered Green Lake County at the intersection of North County Line Road and Proscarian Road (3.78 miles south-southwest of Manchester) and tracked northeast to a point 1.85 miles southeast of Markesan on the Grand River near the southwestern intersection of CTH A and CTH S.  In Green Lake County, this tornado affected only rural areas, and only intermitent tree branch damage was noted in a NWS storm survey.  The beginning and ending lat-lon numbers for this tornado segment in Green Lake County were N43.63221/W89.06693 and N43.69813/W88.95858.  This segment was rated EF0 on the EF-Scale, based on a DI #27, DOD2, with winds of 65 mph (58 knots).

This brief tornado spun up about 3.85 miles west-southwest of the village of Wyocena just east of the intersection of Dunning Road and Patchin Road.  It was captured in a video tape.  Only some damage to tree branches was noted.  The starting and ending lat-lon numbers are N43.47857/W89.37096 and N43.48060/w89.36700. On the EF-Scale, this tornado was given a rating of EF0, based on DI #27 (TH), DOD2.

Young woman succumbed to drowning injuries which occurred at Zoo Beach along the Racine lakefront, shortly after being pulled from the water.  Onshore winds and waves may have caused longshore and structural currents along the beach and North Pier which may have contributed to the drowning. According to witnesses, the young woman was swimming in a shallow area and a underwater current carried her to deep water.  Officials stated the young woman did not know how to swim.

A young teenage swimmer at North Beach along the Racine lakefront was found unconscious about 200 yards from shore. The swimmer was flown to a local hospital but succumbed to injuries sustained from drowning two days later. Onshore winds and waves may have caused long shore and structural currents along North Beach and the North Beach Pier which may have contributed to the drowning death.
